meta.method: 2-round multi-agent audit with adversarial verification; see AUDIT.md section 0
meta.note_on_scratch_paths: Evidence/reproduction text quoted verbatim from each auditing subagent may reference scratchpad/... or /tmp/... paths -- that session's own ephemeral working directory, not anything in this repository. Those files do not persist and are not committed; they are kept in this quoted text only as a record of how each finding was derived. The important references are the repo file:line citations (e.g. src/grnbench/qc.py:100), which remain valid at the audited commit. The most important findings (AUDIT.md sections 3-5) have their key reproduction scripts re-run and committed under repro/ in this folder.

round1_area_findings.title: Top-k Jaccard counts the untied-by-choice missing-prediction block (and zero-weight blocks) as part of the top-k, so two methods with no shared edges show Jaccard 1.000
round1_area_findings.evidence: top_pairs() takes threshold = weight at rank k and keeps every edge with weight >= threshold. top_k_overlap() (metrics.py:293-295) first calls align_rankings(edge_sets, universe), which pads every candidate the method did not predict with weight 0.0, all tied. When a method predicts fewer than k edges, the threshold is 0 and the whole universe lands in its 'top-k'. Reproduced through the CLI (scratchpad/eval/cli.py): universe 10 TFs x 200 genes, methA = universe rows 0-499, methB = rows 1000-1499 (disjoint), `grnbench-eval methA.tsv methB.tsv --gold gold.tsv --universe universe.tsv` (default --overlap-k 1000). eval_report.md prints `| **methA** | - | 1.000 |`, and the JSON has top_k_sizes {'methA': 2000, 'methB': 2000}. With k=40 < n_pred the same lists give 0.0. The same thing happens without a universe for any method that outputs a block of equal zero weights (lasso-like): top_pairs(S1,100) and top_pairs(S2,100), whose 20 nonzero edges are disjoint, give sets of 2000 each and Jaccard 1.0. subsample_stability (stability.py:471) uses the same helper, so a sparse method whose nonzero count is below --stability-top-k is reported as perfectly stable. Neither the Markdown nor the HTML heatmap shows top_k_sizes. The existing test test_overlap_includes_entire_boundary_tie covers only ties the method itself returned, not the padding block.
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: A user compares their own model against built-ins with grnbench-eval --universe, and one list (ARACNe3 after DPI, a top-N plugin output, lasso) has fewer than 1000 edges. The report's 'methods agreeing?' matrix says the methods agree completely (1.000) when they share nothing. The docstring warns about exactly this misreading.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: In top_k_overlap, and in stability with a universe, rank only the predicted edges (align without padding, or drop rows with missing_predictions) before top_pairs. Alternatively, when the boundary block is the padding block or is larger than a declared cap, return NaN with a reason. Always show top_k_sizes next to the Jaccard in the md/html, and add a test with two disjoint short lists plus --universe.
round1_area_findings.vreason:
I reproduced this at HEAD 13106b1 through the library, the CLI and the stability path. The cited line numbers are wrong: universe.py has only 113 lines and stability.py has 75. The defect sits in top_pairs at src/grnbench/eval/universe.py:106-113, where line 111 is `threshold = df.weight.iloc[min(k,len(df))-1]` and line 112 is `head = df[df.weight >= threshold]`. The mechanism is as described. align_ranking (universe.py:78-80) gives every unpredicted universe pair weight 0.0. top_k_overlap (metrics.py:293-295) aligns with the universe and then calls top_pairs. When a method has fewer than k predictions, the rank-k weight is 0, so the whole universe becomes that method's 'top-k'. Two such methods then get Jaccard 1.0 even when their predictions are disjoint.

The 'complete boundary tie' policy is intentional. It is documented in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-13-reliable-benchmark.md:32 and tested in tests/test_eval_contract.py:53 (test_overlap_includes_entire_boundary_tie). That test covers only ties the method returned itself. Nothing documents or accepts the case where the padding block, or a lasso zero block, counts as agreement. That case contradicts what the metric is for: the metrics.py docstring and the HTML caption both say near-zero overlap means the methods do not confirm each other. The Markdown table and the HTML heatmap (html_report.py:202-224, 592-597) show only the Jaccard. top_k_sizes appears only in the JSON.

Reachability: `grnbench run` always passes `--universe candidate_universe.tsv.gz` and `--overlap-k 1000` (cli_run.py:71, 177-179). So in the product's comparison report, any method or user plugin that returns fewer than 1000 edges triggers this. ARACNe3 after DPI and top-N plugins are examples. The stability path works without a universe but gives the same result for the built-in `lasso` method. `lasso` keeps the full regulator x target block with exact zeros (classical.py:194-213, 227-238). If fewer than --stability-top-k coefficients are nonzero, the method is reported as perfectly stable.

Why medium and not higher: real_bench, paper/ and the GUI (src/grnbench/ui) never call top_k_overlap or subsample_stability; I grepped benchmarks/, paper/ and src/grnbench/ui and found no callers. The overlap is also a descriptive diagnostic, not a scored metric. So no headline or confirmatory result is affected, but a main CLI comparison report gives a wrong, opposite-meaning value whenever the trigger above is met. Minimal fix: in top_k_overlap, run top_pairs on the unpadded validated predictions instead of the universe-aligned frames. In top_pairs, or in both callers, return NaN with a reason when the boundary block is the zero/padding block, or when the selected set is much larger than k. Show top_k_sizes in the md/html. Add a test with two disjoint short lists plus a universe, and one with a sparse-zero block.

round1_area_findings.title: real_bench scores a dataset from its surviving contexts when a model fails in only some of them; this contradicts exclusion rule (c) of the confirmatory records and breaks context pairing across models
round1_area_findings.evidence: score_models appends NaN for a context where a method raises and later computes `x = [y for y in v[metric] if np.isfinite(y)]; mean(x)` (lines 213-216). The dataset therefore keeps a finite score averaged over the other contexts. out[f"m_{m}_{arm}_error"] is overwritten per context, so only the last error survives and the number of failed contexts is not recorded. Reproduced (scratchpad/eval/partial_ctx.py): 2 contexts, spearman_signed made to raise on context 2 only. Output: {'m_spearman_signed_baseline_error': 'ValueError: 1 genes have 0 variance', 'm_pearson_signed_baseline_auprc_ratio': 1.237 (mean of 2 contexts), 'm_spearman_signed_baseline_auprc_ratio': 1.007 (context 1 only)}. models_section then pairs these two per-dataset values as if they came from the same data. EXP-20260926-LM-1.md and EXP-20260925-LM-2.md fix exclusion rule (c): 'a dataset where a model errors is dropped from the pairs involving that model only'. In the committed runs, 3/20 datasets have 3-4 contexts in the auto arm ([1,1,1,1,3,1,1,1,1,4,...,3,1,1]). LM-1's only model error was on a 1-context dataset (score NaN), so the published H1/H2 numbers are not affected.
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: On the planned fresh-set confirmatory rerun, a model fails on one per-cell-type context of a multi-context auto arm (e.g. a small context or a degenerate gene; issue #13 was exactly this kind of failure). The dataset silently stays in the primary pair with a partial-context mean instead of being dropped as pre-registered, and the report shows only one error string. For cross-model pairs (e.g. grnboost2 vs pearson_signed) the two per-dataset values come from different context sets.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: If any context of (method, arm) errors, set the dataset score for that method to NaN, as rule (c) states. Also record m_{m}_{arm}_failed_contexts and keep all error messages. Alternatively, amend rule (c) with a D-xxx before the next confirmatory run. Add a test with one failing context out of two.
round1_area_findings.vreason:
The code at HEAD (13106b1) does exactly what the finding says. In benchmarks/real_bench.py score_models, a failing context appends NaN (lines 207-209), and line 215 then averages only the finite values, `x = [y for y in v[metric] if np.isfinite(y)]`. So a dataset where a model fails in 1 of k contexts still gets a finite score from the surviving contexts. Line 210 writes out[f"m_{m}_{arm}_error"] on every failing context, so each new error overwrites the last. Nothing counts failed model contexts. The `{arm}_failed_contexts` field at line 282 counts preprocessing failures only.

models_section (lines 351-404) drops a dataset from a pair only through `mat[[a,b]].dropna()`. It never reads the `_error` columns, and neither does src/grnbench/texreport.py:366, which only lists them. So a partly failed dataset stays in the paired t / Holm family. Its value comes from fewer contexts than the other model's, so the pair no longer compares like with like.

Both confirmatory records pre-register rule (c): "a dataset where a model errors is dropped from the pairs involving that model only, and reported". This is EXP-20260926-LM-1.md lines 32-33 and EXP-20260925-LM-2.md lines 26-27. Neither DECISIONS.md, ATTEMPTS.md nor experiments/README.md documents partial-context averaging, so the code contradicts the pre-registration.

This is reachable. In the committed rows of both LM-1 and LM-2, 3 of 20 datasets have 3 or 4 contexts in the auto arm, which is the primary arm. STATE.md lists a fresh-set rerun of C5 as a next step.

The committed headline numbers are not affected. LM-1's only model errors (RegDiffusion and RegDiffusion_motif) were on the entorhinal-cortex dataset, which has 1 context in both the auto and baseline arms, so its score is NaN and it was dropped correctly (n = 19). LM-2 has no model errors.

Medium, not higher. The specific trigger cited, issue #13 (zero-variance genes in RegDiffusion), is fixed at HEAD: src/grnbench/infer/regdiffusion_adapter.py:30 references #13, and STATE.md says it was fixed in #16. Any other exception in one context of a multi-context arm would still trigger the bug.

One extra gap, same root cause: when auto and baseline point to the same candidate and there is no artifacts_dir, the dedup branch (lines 164-167) copies `block`. `block` does not contain the error key, so the second arm records no error string at all. In my reproduction only `m_spearman_signed_baseline_error` appeared, and the auto arm carried a finite partial score with no error recorded.

The minimal fix is the one the finding proposes. If any context of (method, arm) errors, set that dataset's score to NaN. Record the number of failed model contexts and keep every error message, including inside the dedup block. Add a test with 1 failing context out of 2. Alternatively, amend rule (c) through a D-xxx decision before the next confirmatory run.
round1_area_findings.vrepro:
I wrote my own script, scratchpad/eval-stats-verify-partialctx/repro.py. It builds 2 synthetic contexts of Poisson counts (200 cells x 30 genes) and monkeypatches grnbench.infer.run_method so that spearman_signed raises ValueError on context 2 only. It then calls real_bench.score_models with arms {baseline: cand, auto: cand} and methods [pearson_signed, spearman_signed]. Real output:
m_pearson_signed_auto_auprc_ratio 1.2360 (the mean of both contexts)
m_spearman_signed_auto_auprc_ratio 1.5565 (context 1 only)
m_spearman_signed_baseline_auprc_ratio 1.5565
m_spearman_signed_baseline_error ValueError: 1 genes have 0 variance
There was no m_spearman_signed_auto_error key: the dedup arm lost the error.
Unpatched, per context: ctx0 pearson 1.0263, spearman 1.5565; ctx1 pearson 1.4458, spearman 1.4134. So spearman's 1.5565 is ctx0 alone, while pearson's 1.236 is the mean of ctx0 and ctx1.
Fed into models_section, the dataset keeps n = 3 for both models, with finite per-dataset values and only an entry under "Model errors".
Committed rows: EXP-20260926-LM-1 auto_n_contexts = [1,1,1,1,3,1,1,1,1,4,1,1,1,1,1,1,1,3,1,1], and baseline is all 1. LM-2 has the same values. LM-1's only model errors are on cxg__10x-3-v2__homo-sapiens__entorhinal-cortex__06b91002 (auto_n_contexts = 1, baseline_n_contexts = 1), with auprc_ratio NaN, so the published H1/H2 numbers are unaffected. LM-2 has no model errors.
Code lines read: real_bench.py 164-167 (dedup), 190-210 (the per-context try/except and the error overwrite), 213-216 (the finite-only mean), 378 (the dropna pairing) and 407 (the error listing).

round1_area_findings.title: With --universe, identifier_overlap always reports 'case-mismatch' for non-uppercase symbols because it compares the raw gold against the already-uppercased universe
round1_area_findings.evidence: load_universe() returns canonical_pairs(), which uppercases everything when not case-sensitive. cli_eval then passes `candidates = universe` to identifier_overlap(candidates, gold_index), and that function compares against gold_index.pairs in raw case (metrics.py:90-98). Reproduced (scratchpad/eval/cli2.py) with universe and gold both written in MGI case (Pou5f1, Sox2, Nanog, GeneN). stderr: `[GOLD CASE] methA: gene symbols differ in case between the edge list and gold 'gold' (0 pairs match exactly, 15 case-insensitively)`. JSON: verdict 'case-mismatch', shared_genes_case_sensitive 0, example_edge_genes ['GENE0',...]. The same files without --universe give verdict 'ok'.
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: Any mouse or MGI-case evaluation run with --universe (the recommended mode) prints a false warning and a red CASE-MISMATCH badge in the HTML, saying the edge list and gold disagree on case when they are identical. Scores are unaffected, but the diagnostic built for exactly this situation becomes noise.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: Run identifier_overlap on the raw edge list (edges), or on the universe file read without case folding, instead of the canonicalized universe. Or have load_universe keep the original spelling alongside the canonical pairs.
round1_area_findings.vreason: The code at HEAD shows the bug without ambiguity. load_universe (src/grnbench/eval/universe.py:54-58) returns canonical_pairs(), which uppercases every identifier when case_sensitive is False (lines 23-28). cli_eval.py:338 sets candidates = universe, and line 343 passes that to identifier_overlap. identifier_overlap (metrics.py:90-98) deliberately compares candidate strings against GoldIndex.pairs, which holds the raw, unfolded gold. So an MGI-case gold can never match exactly against an uppercased universe, and folded > exact always gives 'case-mismatch'. I reproduced this independently with my own inputs, and the control run without --universe says 'ok'. Nothing in tests/, docs/ or .projectos documents this as intended: tests only cover identifier_overlap on raw edges. Scores are unaffected: the AUPRC is the same and the coverage table correctly shows 12/12 gold reachable. Only the diagnostic (stderr warning, JSON verdict, md table and HTML badge) is wrong, so low severity is right. No real_bench or confirmatory path calls identifier_overlap; the only caller is the grnbench-eval CLI.
round1_area_findings.vrepro: In scratchpad/eval-stats-adv/f1 I built an 8-gene MGI-case universe (all 56 ordered pairs), a 12-pair gold and a scored edge list, all in MGI case (Pou5f1, Sox2, ...). `grnbench-eval methA.tsv --gold gold.tsv --universe universe.tsv --skip-nulls` gave: - stderr: "[GOLD CASE] methA: gene symbols differ in case between the edge list and gold 'gold' (0 pairs match exactly, 12 case-insensitively)." - JSON identifiers: {verdict: 'case-mismatch', matched_pairs_case_sensitive: 0, matched_pairs_case_insensitive: 12, shared_genes_case_sensitive: 0, example_edge_genes: ['ESRRB','KLF4','NANOG','POU5F1','SALL4'], example_gold_genes: ['Esrrb','Klf4',...], scope: 'candidate-universe'} - HTML: `CASE-MISMATCH` The same run without --universe gave verdict 'ok', 12/12 exact. Gold reachability was 12/12 in both runs, so scores are unaffected.

round1_area_findings.title: Claims and generated captions call the test 'two-sided' but the code runs one-sided directed tests with Holm over both directions; the quoted p_Holm is not the p of the named test
round1_area_findings.evidence: compare_units computes p_a_gt_b = t.sf((mean-margin)/se) and p_b_gt_a = t.sf((-mean-margin)/se), which are one-sided, and Holm-adjusts over 2 x n_pairs directed hypotheses. C4/C5 say 'paired two-sided t, Holm over 4 declared hypotheses (p = 1.2e-6 ...)'. texreport.py:277 writes 'two-sided per direction' into every comparisons_*.tex caption, and the records say the same. Recomputed from benchmarks/results/EXP-20260926-LM-1/rows with scipy/statsmodels (scratchpad/eval/check_h.py and the follow-up run): one-sided p over the 4 directed hypotheses, Holm-adjusted, gives [3.63e-10, 1, 1.18e-06, 1], which is what the code reports. Two-sided paired t with Holm over the 2 pairs gives [3.63e-10, 7.87e-07]. Every reported number (diff, CI, n, p_Holm) matches my independent recomputation for LM-1 and LM-2. Only the label of the procedure is wrong, and the reported p is conservative.
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer reruns 'paired two-sided t, Holm over the declared pairs' as written and gets p = 7.9e-07 for RegDiffusion instead of 1.2e-06, and flags a reproducibility discrepancy in a claim that is otherwise exactly reproducible.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: Describe the procedure as 'paired t, one-sided in each direction, Holm over the 2 x pairs directed hypotheses (equivalent to controlling directional FWER)' in CLAIMS.md C1/C4/C5, the records and the texreport caption. Alternatively, switch to a two-sided test per pair, which requires a new D-xxx since it changes the registered test.
round1_area_findings.vreason:
compare_units (src/grnbench/eval/comparison.py:82-83) computes pa = t.sf((mean-margin)/se) and pb = t.sf((-mean-margin)/se): each is one-sided. texreport.comparisons (lines 151-172) calls compare_units once per pair and applies holm_adjust over all 2*pairs directed p-values. Yet texreport.py:277 hard-codes 'two-sided per direction' into every caption. CLAIMS.md C1/C4/C5 say 'paired two-sided t, Holm over N declared hypotheses', and records EXP-20260925-LM-2:32/74 and EXP-20260926-LM-1:39/113 say the same.

The reported p values match none of the readings the label suggests. Two-sided Holm over the 2 pairs gives 7.87e-7. Two-sided p for each of the 4 directed hypotheses with Holm gives 1.57e-6. The code gives 1.18e-6. Only 'one-sided per direction, Holm over 4 directed hypotheses' reproduces the published numbers.

Mitigating factors:
- The pre-registration names compare_units and '4 directed hypotheses', so a rerun from the record's code path reproduces the numbers exactly.
- The directional-Holm procedure is conservative relative to two-sided Holm, so no decision changes.
- D-008 and A-006 describe the procedure correctly ('Holm-corrects both directions of every pair') without saying 'two-sided'.

The label 'two-sided' is still factually wrong in claim text and generated captions, so this is confirmed at low severity.

round1_area_findings.title: Claim C3 asserts equivalence ('ties ... for every model') from untested, unresolved differences
round1_area_findings.evidence: C3: 'On real data the engine's automatic cleaning ties with a fixed baseline pipeline for every model tested.' Its evidence table paper/tables/T_models_real_EXP-20260925-LM-1.md contains only descriptive 'auto > baseline' counts (0/12 to 3/12) and means. No auto-vs-baseline test and no equivalence margin were run. In test12/all_rows_real.csv, 8/12 datasets have auto_candidate == baseline, so the scores are identical by construction. The other 4 are simply untested. The project rule (.projectos/STATE.md:47, D-0xx for grnbench compare) is 'Unresolved != equivalent'. EXP-20260925-LM-1.md:38 uses the same wording ('auto vs baseline cleaning ties').
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: If C3 is promoted (e.g. into the product/paper narrative that cleaning 'does not matter' on real data), it states an equivalence that no analysis supports. Its status is only draft today.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: Reword to what was measured: 'the automatic pipeline selected the baseline pipeline in 8/12 datasets; on the remaining datasets, differences were not tested / not resolved'. For an equivalence claim, pre-register a margin and run TOST via compare_units(margin=...).
round1_area_findings.vreason:
CLAIMS.md:19 C3 reads 'the engine's automatic cleaning ties with a fixed baseline pipeline for every model tested', which is an equivalence statement.

The cited evidence does not support it:
- The evidence table T_models_real_EXP-20260925-LM-1.md only has descriptive 'auto > baseline' counts and means. No auto-vs-baseline test or equivalence margin is declared.
- The second cited record, EXP-20260924-PRE-2, itself calls the real part 'inconclusive'.
- The project rule is 'Unresolved != equivalent' (STATE.md:47, D-008, compare_units returns unresolved_is_equivalent False).

In the committed test12 rows, 8/12 datasets have auto_candidate == 'baseline', so those scores are identical by construction. Among the 4 datasets where auto picked something else, grnboost2's AUPRC ratio is lower in all 4, with raw one-sided p(baseline > auto) = 0.043 over n = 12. That is unadjusted and not a registered test, but it shows the 'ties for every model' wording is not even descriptively robust.

The claim is draft and exploratory, so severity stays low. It is still a claim-evidence mismatch in the claims ledger.

round1_area_findings.title: Regulator list is chosen from the full CollecTRI reference, so the selection/evaluation split is crossed; C4/C5 claim text leaves this condition out
round1_area_findings.evidence: real_bench.py:74-90 `_reference()` keeps the MAX_TFS=150 TFs with the highest degree in the FULL CollecTRI (both halves). Line 250 `tfs = sorted({s for s, _ in pairs})` is then passed as `tf_list` to `screen_candidates` and to `score_models`, where it sets the models' regulators and the evaluation universe (`sources = resolve_tf_names(genes, tfs)`). The split only happens afterwards, in screen.py:245 `split_reference`, which is balanced per TF (screen.py:36-47). So each TF's evaluation-half degree is floor or ceil of half its full degree, and 'top-150 by full degree' is in effect 'top-150 by evaluation-half degree'. I ran split_reference on a synthetic 600-TF heavy-tailed reference: `per-TF eval degree == floor(full/2): True`; `overlap top150(full) vs top150(eval half): 148`. paper/REPORTING_CHECKLIST.md:18 requires the split to be 'never crossed'. The C4/C5 sentences in paper/CLAIMS.md:16-17 do not mention that only the regulators with the most evaluation-reference targets were scored. The records list the setting only under 'seeds' and do not say it uses the evaluation half.
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: Both arms of each pair share the same TF set, so the paired sign is not biased by construction. But the population the lift is measured on (the best-annotated TFs, where a motif prior is most likely to agree with literature curation) is chosen with evaluation-half information. The C4/C5 sentences would read in the paper as a general motif-prior effect. The LM-1 secondary endpoint 'mean AUPRC ratio against random' is also conditioned on this selection.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: Choose regulators without the evaluation half: top-k by selection-half degree, or a reference-independent TF catalogue expressed in the data. Rerun as a new pre-registered experiment. Until then, add the condition ('among the 150 TFs with most CollecTRI targets, selected on the full reference') to C4/C5 and to the records' deviation or limitation notes, and do not tick checklist line 18.
round1_area_findings.vreason:
The auditor read the code correctly: `_reference()` (benchmarks/real_bench.py:74-90) keeps the top MAX_TFS=150 TFs by degree in the full CollecTRI reference, and `split_reference` (src/grnbench/screen.py:36-47) runs afterwards. Calling this leakage or a crossed split is still wrong, for four reasons.

(1) The full-reference ranking tells the TF choice nothing about the evaluation half that the selection half does not already tell it. `split_reference` splits each TF's edges evenly, so each TF's selection-half degree is ceil(n/2), which rises with the full degree n. Ranking by full degree is therefore the same as ranking by selection-half degree, except that the ceiling creates ties that full degree breaks. My reproduction ran the auditor's own proposed fix (split the whole reference first, then take the top 150 by selection-half degree). Over 20 synthetic heavy-tailed references it picks the same TFs, 146 to 150 of 150 (mean 148.15). The only swaps are between TFs of degree 2k-1 and 2k at the cutoff. So the fix would leave the scored population and the C4/C5 numbers essentially unchanged. The concern that the TFs are 'chosen with evaluation-half information' applies just as much to a choice made from the selection half alone. What remains is a scope choice (score the TFs with the most known targets), not leakage.

(2) The choice is intentional, documented and pre-registered:
- real_bench.py:43-46 explains the power and runtime reasons and says 'A bench setting, reported as such'.
- docs/models_that_work.md:47 lists 'TF list (regulator set)' as an allowed prior: 'the 150 CollecTRI TFs with most targets in the data, identical for every method'.
- Both confirmatory records fix it before the run: EXP-20260925-LM-2.md:41-42 and EXP-20260926-LM-1.md:49-50 ('regulators = the 150 TFs with most reference targets in the data (MAX_TFS)'). 'Reference targets' here means the full CollecTRI, so the records do disclose it.

round1_area_findings.title: score_models keeps a dataset scored on the surviving contexts when a model fails in only some contexts, which contradicts registered exclusion rule (c); latent, not triggered in LM-2/LM-1
round1_area_findings.evidence:
Lines 214-216: `x = [y for y in v[metric] if np.isfinite(y)]; block[...] = float(np.mean(x)) if x else np.nan`. A failing context is dropped from the mean, only an `_error` string is logged, and models_section later keeps the dataset in every pair. Both registrations say: '(c) a dataset where a model errors is dropped from the pairs involving that model only'. Reproduction (scratch demo, 3 contexts, pearson_signed forced to fail in context 2, real score_models + evaluate_ranking) printed:
m_pearson_signed_baseline_auprc_ratio 1.830381187440011
m_pearson_signed_baseline_error ValueError: simulated failure in one context
m_spearman_signed_baseline_auprc_ratio 2.3665362604371896
The failing model still gets a finite dataset score (2 contexts) and is compared with one averaged over 3. Checked in the committed rows: the only model errors are RegDiffusion on the entorhinal dataset, which has 1 context (auto/baseline n_contexts = 1), so neither confirmatory result is affected.
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: In any multi-context dataset (per-cell-type contexts are small, and a constant gene after subsampling is the failure already seen), a partial model failure silently changes that dataset's unit score and keeps it in the paired test, against the pre-registered rule. For cross-model pairs (e.g. regdiffusion vs pearson_signed), A and B are then averaged over different context sets.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: If any context of a model errors, set that model's dataset score (per arm) to NaN so the pair drops it, and record n_contexts_scored per model. Add a test with a partial-context failure.
round1_area_findings.vreason:
I checked this at HEAD 13106b1 and it holds. In benchmarks/real_bench.py, lines 207-211 turn a failing context into NaN plus an `m_{m}_{arm}_error` string. Lines 215-216 then average only the finite contexts (`x = [y for y in v[metric] if np.isfinite(y)]; ... float(np.mean(x)) if x else np.nan`). So the model still gets a finite dataset score whenever at least one context succeeds. models_section (lines 376-381) runs `mat[[a,b]].dropna()`, so that dataset stays in every pair that involves the model.

This goes against the registered rule. EXP-20260925-LM-2.md lines 26-27 and EXP-20260926-LM-1.md lines 32-33 both say: "(c) a dataset where a model errors is dropped from the pairs involving that model only, and reported". Nothing documents the partial case as intended. I searched DECISIONS.md, ATTEMPTS.md, experiments/README.md, the records and docs/. No test covers score_models either.

The path can be reached in the confirmatory setup. The auto arm has 3-4 contexts in 3 of the 20 datasets (`auto_n_contexts` is 3, 4 and 3 for primary-motor-cortex, lung and smart-seq2 cerebral cortex). The failure type has already happened: RegDiffusion's zero-variance gene after subsampling, issue #13.

One point in the finding needs a correction. For the H1/H2 within-model pairs (X_motif vs X), both members fail in the same contexts. A failed base is never cached (lines 193-196), so X_motif re-runs it and fails in the same context. Those pairs are therefore still averaged over the same context set. They still break rule (c), because the dataset is kept rather than dropped. The mismatched context sets only hit cross-model pairs (e.g. regdiffusion vs pearson_signed) or a failure in the motif step alone.

The committed results are not affected. In EXP-20260926-LM-1 the only model errors are RegDiffusion on entorhinal-cortex 06b91002, which has auto_n_contexts = baseline_n_contexts = 1, so its score is NaN and the dataset was dropped correctly (n = 19). EXP-20260925-LM-2 has no model errors. Medium is the right severity: a latent departure from the pre-registered exclusion rule with a clear trigger, and no effect on any headline number.

Side observation, not part of this finding: when artifacts_dir is None and auto == baseline (the dedup path, line 164), the error string is written only under the first arm's key. My reproduction shows `m_pearson_signed_baseline_error` but no `m_pearson_signed_auto_error`. So the failure is reported under the baseline label only. LM-1 ran with KEEP_ARTIFACTS=1, which turns dedup off, so it was not affected.

round1_area_findings.title: Claim C3 asserts equivalence ('ties') with no equivalence test and intervals too wide to support it
round1_area_findings.evidence: C3: 'On real data the engine's automatic cleaning ties with a fixed baseline pipeline for every model tested.' The cited table (paper/tables/T_models_real_EXP-20260925-LM-1.md) has no auto-vs-baseline test and no margin, and EXP-20260925-LM-1.md:38 just asserts 'auto vs baseline cleaning ties'. My 95% t intervals for auto minus baseline (AUPRC ratio) from the committed test12 rows: pearson_signed +0.0021 [-0.0593, +0.0635] (per-dataset range -0.247..+0.196); spearman_signed [-0.0535, +0.0603]; regdiffusion [-0.0511, +0.0543]. The plausible differences are about a third of the headline motif lift (0.18-0.23). In 12/20 LM-2 datasets auto == baseline by construction (the engine chose the baseline), which counts as a 'tie' trivially. The project's own rules (STATE 'Unresolved != equivalent', REPORTING_CHECKLIST 'unresolved is reported as unresolved, not as no difference', compare_units `unresolved_is_equivalent: False`) forbid this wording.
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: The sentence, drafted 'as it would read in the paper', turns an unresolved comparison into a claim of no difference about the product's core feature.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: Reword to 'auto vs baseline cleaning is unresolved (no equivalence margin declared)', citing the intervals. If equivalence is the claim, pre-register a margin and run a TOST / interval-inclusion test.

The 'ties' wording goes back to hand-written summaries: EXP-20260925-LM-1.md line 38 and REPORT.md:117 ('still ties ... pearson_motif 1.547 vs 1.538'); REPORT.md:31 adds 'differenze < 0.01'. Those summaries use a difference of means with no interval and no margin. The ledger row also contradicts one of its own cited records: EXP-20260924-PRE-2's verdict is 'real inconclusive'. round1_area_findings.title: Motif-prior lift in pooled AUPRC ratio is confounded by a TF-level ordering (min over annotated motifs, motif-less TFs tied last); no control separates it from target-level sequence evidence
round1_area_findings.evidence: motif_ranks() gives each TF x gene pair `ranks[rr].min(0)` over all motifs annotated to the TF (line 289), then `np.minimum` over databases (line 290). A TF with no motif gets `n_total` for every gene (line 283). motif_rank_product() (316-325) combines this with the base rank and never normalises per TF. So the prior ranks whole TFs by how many motifs they have: the expected minimum of k random ranks is about N/(k+1). The primary endpoint pools AUPRC over all TFs. Because split_reference is balanced per TF, each TF's evaluation-half degree equals its CollecTRI degree / 2, so any TF-level ordering that tracks CollecTRI degree raises pooled AUPRC with no information about targets. Reproduction: scratchpad/harness/tf_level_confound.py uses fake cisTarget rankings that are pure random permutations (no target information), expression that is Poisson noise, and 60 TFs with 0-50 motifs. Output: `degree ~ n_motifs (study bias): pearson_signed AUPRC ratio 1.021 | pearson_motif 1.367 | motif_prior 1.577 (prevalence 0.1237, n_candidates 39540 in all arms)`; `degree independent of n_motifs: 1.000 | 0.982 | 0.974`. With a moderate link (tf_level_confound2.py, Spearman(k, degree) = 0.51): `0.998 -> 1.063`. With motif presence only (15/60 TFs without a motif, half the degree): `1.043 -> 1.103`. Committed real data shows the same signature: in the LM-2 tf_recovery TSVs (top-30 TFs, hits@20 within each TF), motif_prior gets 24/41/22 hits vs pearson_signed 26/49/27 on 06b91002/df287f8d/b94e3bdf, yet its pooled AUPRC ratio is higher (1.511/1.231/1.504 vs 1.307/1.184/1.385) and its EPR much lower (1.20/1.39/1.19 vs 2.02/1.77/2.52). That is consistent with a between-TF component. Counter-evidence: in the same tables pearson_motif and grnboost2_motif gain within-TF hits (26->31, 49->55, 27->29; 16->24, 25->36, 13->19), so part of the lift is plausibly target-level. The design cannot tell the two apart. Neither the records, DECISIONS, ATTEMPTS nor CLAIMS mention this, while docs/models_that_work.md reads the lift as 'sequence: whether the TF's binding motif sits near the target' and the LM-2 verdict says 'expression adds to sequence'.
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: CollecTRI degree tracks how well studied a TF is, and so does the number of cisTarget motif annotations (direct, similarity and orthology). The rank product then moves well-annotated TFs up as blocks. The pooled AUPRC ratio (the primary endpoint of EXP-20260925-LM-2 and EXP-20260926-LM-1) rises even where the motif carries no target-specific signal. C4/C5 and the docs attribute that rise to motif sites near targets, and the committed evidence cannot support that attribution.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: Add a registered control arm, e.g. `motif_prior_tfperm`: each TF's motif-rank row permuted across genes (keeps the TF-level rank distribution, removes target identity). Also report a within-TF metric (mean over TFs of the per-TF AUPRC ratio on the evaluation half) as a secondary endpoint. Optionally rank motif scores within each TF before the rank product. Until then, state in C4/C5 and in the records that the lift is not shown to be target-level.
round1_area_findings.vreason:
I confirmed the mechanism in the code at 13106b1.
- `motif_ranks` sets each TF x gene to `ranks[rr].min(0)` over every motif annotated to the TF (cistarget.py:289). The annotation includes direct, similarity and orthology rows, since `load_annotation` keeps them all (lines 95-101).
- It takes `np.minimum` across databases (line 290). A TF with no motif keeps `n_total` for every gene (line 283).
- `motif_rank_product` (316-325) pools the motif ranks over all edges and never normalises them per TF.
- The endpoint is pooled over the universe `sources x genes` (real_bench.py:179, 204). `split_reference` (screen.py:36-47) halves each TF's edges, so each TF's evaluation-half degree follows its CollecTRI degree.

The motif prior therefore moves whole TFs up or down by how many motifs they have. Pooled AUPRC rewards any TF-level order that tracks reference degree.

Nothing documents this. It is not in DECISIONS, ATTEMPTS or the LM-2 / 26-LM-1 records. The records and CLAIMS give no row-permuted control and no within-TF endpoint.

I reproduced the effect twice:
1. I reran the auditor's script and got the reported numbers exactly.
2. I wrote an independent version that is harder to trigger. Motifs within a TF are correlated, as clustered motifs are. Motif counts are heavy-tailed and 8 of 80 TFs have no motif. The link between motif count and degree is only moderate, and the motif rankings carry no target information.

With Spearman 0.42 between motif count and degree, the pooled AUPRC ratio of Pearson plus motif rose by about 0.10 with zero target information. A control that shuffles each TF's motif row across genes kept almost all of that lift. So a between-TF component of the size seen on real data (+0.13 to +0.18) is possible, and the registered design cannot separate it from a target-level effect.

Why medium and not higher:
1. C4 and C5 as written in `paper/CLAIMS.md` say only that adding the prior raises the AUPRC ratio on the evaluation half. That statement is literally supported, and no committed number is wrong.
2. The only mechanistic wording is a rationale sentence in `docs/models_that_work.md` (lines 39-41). The LM-2 phrase "expression adds to sequence" compares `pearson_motif` with `motif_prior`, which carry the same TF-level component, so that phrase is unaffected.
3. The real-data link between motif count and CollecTRI degree cannot be checked here: the cisTarget and CollecTRI files are not local.
4. The committed within-TF evidence points to a real target-level part. In `motif_lift_*.tsv`, summed hits@20 over 150 TFs rise in all 8 dataset x model cases (Pearson 55->58, 79->97, 52->58; GRNBoost2 33->45, 53->79, 29->42; RegDiffusion 91->98, 64->67).

The auditor's "real-data signature" is weak. `motif_prior` has lower top-30 hits@20 and lower EPR than `pearson_signed` but a higher AUPRC ratio. In the synthetic confound, however, EPR rises too, so this pattern does not single out a TF-level cause.

Conclusion: the confound and the missing control are real and reproducible. They put the paper's interpretation of the headline at risk, but they do not invalidate C4 or C5 as worded.

round1_area_findings.title: A model that fails in some contexts of a dataset keeps a finite dataset score averaged over fewer contexts, which breaks registered exclusion rule (c) and the pairing
round1_area_findings.evidence: score_models appends NaN for a failed method/context (lines 207-210), then averages only the finite contexts: `x = [y for y in v[metric] if np.isfinite(y)]; block[...] = float(np.mean(x)) if x else np.nan` (215-216). Only the last error message is kept (`out[f"m_{m}_{arm}_error"]`). models_section then pairs the two per-dataset means with `mat[[a_name, b_name]].dropna()`. Reproduction: scratchpad/harness/partial_context.py has two contexts and spearman_signed forced to fail in ctx1 only. Output: `m_pearson_signed_auto_auprc_ratio 13.3516` (= mean of ctx0 13.372 and ctx1 13.331), `m_spearman_signed_auto_auprc_ratio 13.3141` (= ctx0 only), `m_spearman_signed_auto_error RuntimeError: context-specific failure`. The dataset stays in the pair with mismatched context sets. The registered rule (EXP-20260925-LM-2 and EXP-20260926-LM-1, rule c) is 'a dataset where a model errors is dropped from the pairs involving that model only'. Committed results are not affected: all errors in the rows are whole-dataset errors, and the multi-context datasets 9b686bb6 (3 ctx), 62315937 (4) and 774c18c5 (3) have no model errors.
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: On a dataset whose auto arm is per cell type (3-4 contexts in 3/20 registered datasets), a context-specific failure is enough to trigger this. Examples: RegDiffusion's zero-variance error before #13, a motif lookup IndexError, a GRNBoost2 failure on a tiny context. The dataset then enters the paired t test with the failing model scored on a different, smaller subset of cell types than its pair partner. Rule (c) is violated without warning, and the paired difference mixes a context effect with a model effect.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: In score_models, record the number of failed contexts per model and arm (`m_{m}_{arm}_failed_contexts`). Either set the dataset score to NaN when any context failed, which implements rule (c), or compute pair means only over contexts where both members are finite (store per-context values in the row). Add a test with a one-context failure.
round1_area_findings.vreason:
The code at HEAD 13106b1 does what the finding says. In benchmarks/real_bench.py, score_models appends NaN for a failed method/context (lines 207-210) and then averages only the finite contexts (lines 213-216): `x = [y for y in v[metric] if np.isfinite(y)]; block[...] = float(np.mean(x)) if x else np.nan`. It keeps only the last error string per model and arm. models_section (lines 375-383) then keeps a dataset in a pair whenever both per-dataset means are finite (`mat[[a_name, b_name]].dropna()`).

Both registered records say the metric is the 'mean over contexts within a dataset' (LM-2 line 13, LM-1 line 15). Both also fix rule (c): 'a dataset where a model errors is dropped from the pairs involving that model only, and reported' (LM-2 lines 26-27, LM-1 lines 32-33). A partially failed model is reported, because the error string does appear under 'Model errors', but it is not dropped. That contradicts the registered rule.

I found nothing in DECISIONS.md, ATTEMPTS.md, the records or the tests that documents averaging over the surviving contexts as intended. No test exercises score_models at all.

Committed results are not affected, which I checked directly. In both EXP-20260925-LM-2 and EXP-20260926-LM-1, the only multi-context datasets are 9b686bb6 (auto has 3 contexts), 62315937 (4) and 774c18c5 (3). None of them has any m_*_error key. The only model errors are the whole-dataset RegDiffusion failures on 06b91002, which are NaN in every arm and correctly excluded. So this is latent, not a blocker. It triggers whenever a model fails in only some contexts of a per-cell-type auto arm, for example on a reproduction or a new confirmatory run. Medium is the right severity.

One correction to the finding's wording: 'mismatched context sets' is only partly true. When the base model fails in a context, run_method raises and nothing is cached, so the _motif variant re-runs the base and fails in the same context. For a pair like (regdiffusion_motif, regdiffusion), both members are then averaged over the same subset. That still breaks rule (c) and the registered 'mean over contexts' metric, but the pair itself stays matched. The context sets really do differ in two cases: a failure only in the combiner (motif_rank_product or cistarget_rerank inside the try block), which hits the pearson_motif vs pearson_signed pair from LM-2's H1, and the cross-model pairs (grnboost2 vs pearson_signed, regdiffusion vs pearson_signed). The suggested fix is sound. The minimal version is to set the dataset score to NaN when any context of that model and arm failed, and to record `m_{m}_{arm}_failed_contexts`.

round1_area_findings.title: Resumable runners freeze transient error rows and cannot tell code versions apart: a resubmission skips them, rows carry no commit, and CODE_COMMIT is overwritten with the last submission's commit
round1_area_findings.evidence: `_run_and_save`: `if path.exists(): return task["id"], "skipped"` (real_bench.py 332-334; the same in engine_bench.py 227-229). run_real_task catches every exception into row['error'] (321-323), so infrastructure errors (disk full, permissions) are written as final rows. Reproduction (scratchpad/harness/resume_skip.py): a row containing `OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device` gives `('cxg__a', 'skipped')` on rerun. The row keys include no commit or version field (98 keys in the LM-1 rows, none about code). hpc/engine_bench.sbatch:59 runs `[ -f GIT_COMMIT ] && cp GIT_COMMIT "$OUT/CODE_COMMIT"` on every submission: it overwrites with the newest commit, and leaves a stale file if GIT_COMMIT is absent. The sbatch header advertises this as 'Resumable: ... resubmitting the same array only runs what is missing'. EXP-20260926-LM-1 deviation 1 (job 670900: 20 error rows from a full /tmp) needed the rows to be moved by hand; the tooling would otherwise have skipped all 20 datasets.
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: A job times out or hits an infrastructure error after some datasets. The code is then fixed (as with #13) and the job resubmitted to the same OUT. The rows from the old code, including the error rows, are kept and silently mixed with rows from the new code, and CODE_COMMIT names only the new commit. The report and the record then cite one commit for results produced by two. Rule (d) of LM-1 depends on the operator noticing.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: Write the commit (GIT_COMMIT or `git rev-parse HEAD`) and the grnbench version into every row. In `report()`, refuse to aggregate rows from more than one commit unless an explicit flag is given. Do not skip rows whose `error` is set unless `--keep-errors` is passed, or move them to `rows_failed/`. In the sbatch, refuse to start if `$OUT/CODE_COMMIT` exists and differs from GIT_COMMIT.
round1_area_findings.vreason:
The code does what the finding says, but the harm it describes is overstated, so I lower it from medium to low.

Confirmed at HEAD 13106b1:
(1) `_run_and_save` skips any task whose row file exists, including a row whose `error` is an infrastructure error (benchmarks/real_bench.py:332-334; the same in engine_bench.py:227-229).
(2) Rows carry no commit or version field. The 98 keys of the LM-1 rows include no commit, version, code or git key.
(3) hpc/engine_bench.sbatch:59 overwrites `$OUT/CODE_COMMIT` on every submission and never checks it against the existing file. When GIT_COMMIT is missing it keeps the stale file, while the log prints 'code unknown'. texreport.py:403 then prints that single file as the run's 'code commit (run folder)'.

Why it is not medium:
(a) Skipping existing rows, error rows included, is intentional and documented. The sbatch header says 'resubmitting ... only runs what is missing'. .claude/skills/grnbench-hpc/SKILL.md section 8 says 'The runners skip datasets whose rows/<task>.json exists; delete a row file only to recompute that dataset on purpose'. Error rows are not silent either: `report()` prints 'errors: N' (real_bench.py:424-430), and the pairs print n per pair. The finding's own example, LM-1 deviation 1, shows the documented procedure working: the rows were moved, the same code 84f28e1 was resubmitted, and the job ended with 0 errors.
(b) The failure scenario ('code is then fixed (as with #13) and the job resubmitted to the same OUT') breaks written rules. experiments/README rule 5 says a rerun is a new experiment ID. AGENTS.md section 7 says never rerun silently. LM-1 exclusion rule (d) says 'one resubmission of the same commit'. The LM-1 record says the #13 rows 'are not rerun'.
(c) No committed result is affected. LM-1 CODE_COMMIT is 84f28e1, the code of both jobs 670900 and 670902. LM-2 had no resubmission.

What remains is a real but small gap. The tooling meant to pin provenance (CODE_COMMIT) records one commit per folder, overwrites it silently and never checks it. A plausible slip is enough to trigger it: `hpc.sh sync` of another branch into the user's one shared cluster checkout between a TIMEOUT and the 'resubmit the same command' step. The rows would then be attributed to the newer commit alone. The fix is cheap: in the sbatch, refuse to start when `$OUT/CODE_COMMIT` exists and differs from GIT_COMMIT, or when GIT_COMMIT is missing. Optionally, write the commit into each row.

round1_area_findings.title: Partial non-independence between the cisTarget motif prior and CollecTRI is undisclosed in the confirmatory records and claims, and the code docstrings assert non-circularity
round1_area_findings.evidence: cistarget.py:34-37: 'No curated TF -> target collection (CollecTRI, DoRothEA, TRRUST) enters here, so scoring against CollecTRI stays non-circular.' base.py:320 says the same. docs/models_that_work.md:52-54 states the opposite caveat: 'some CollecTRI edges were curated from papers that used motif evidence, so motif priors and CollecTRI are not fully independent evidence'. CollecTRI also integrates DoRothEA A, whose evidence classes include TFBS predictions. grep finds no mention of this dependence in experiments/EXP-20260925-LM-2.md, experiments/EXP-20260926-LM-1.md or paper/CLAIMS.md (C4, C5). paper/REPORTING_CHECKLIST.md:19 requires 'no circularity (a prior used by a model is not the evaluation reference)'.
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: C4/C5 are presented as a motif lift measured against an independent reference. Part of the agreement may come from CollecTRI edges supported by motif/TFBS evidence, and the headline claims do not tell the reader so.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: Add the caveat to both records and to C4/C5. Soften the docstrings to 'no curated edge is read; partial evidence overlap exists'. Optionally add a sensitivity analysis that scores against CollecTRI edges not supported by DoRothEA-A/TFBS-derived resources (decoupler's CollecTRI table carries a per-edge resources column).
round1_area_findings.vreason: The docstrings are accurate under the project's own definition of circularity. paper/REPORTING_CHECKLIST.md:19 defines it as 'a prior used by a model is not the evaluation reference', and cistarget.py reads only motif rankings and motif-to-TF annotations. No CollecTRI, DoRothEA or TRRUST edge enters. The residual evidence overlap is an intentional, documented design judgement: docs/models_that_work.md:52-54, the design doc for these same models, states it and classes it as 'biology, not leakage: no edge of the evaluation half is read by any method'. So the docstrings and the doc do not contradict each other. The doc says both things, and the docstrings repeat only the part that is literally true. C4 and C5 in paper/CLAIMS.md are worded as measured lifts 'on the CollecTRI evaluation half'. Neither says the reference is independent of motif evidence (grep for 'independent'/'non-circular' finds only the two docstrings and the design doc). The committed numbers support the claims as written. The finding does not show that the overlap inflates the lift. It is a general caveat about CollecTRI provenance, and I cannot check the CollecTRI/DoRothEA-A TFBS provenance offline. Adding the caveat to the paper's discussion, or running a sensitivity analysis on non-TFBS-supported edges, would improve the paper, but the absence is not a defect in code, numbers or claims.

round1_area_findings.title: data_manifest.py --check exits 0 when files listed in the manifest are missing
round1_area_findings.evidence: check() iterates only over the files present under DATA_ROOT (`for f in sorted(p for p in root.rglob('*') ...)`). Rows of the manifest with no file are never reported. Reproduction: build a manifest over two datasets, delete one folder, run `--check`. Output: `ok=1 ok-eol=0 MISMATCH=0 UNLISTED=0`, `exit=0`. EXP-20260926-LM-1 uses this check as its data gate ('must exit 0: 50 files'), and its exclusion rule (a) needs failed downloads to be reported as missing.
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: A download fails and leaves no file (e.g. an interrupted `fetch_cellxgene.py --from-manifest`). The check still exits 0, `real_bench plan` just produces fewer tasks, and the missing dataset is noticed only if someone compares counts by hand.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: Report MISSING for every manifest row under the checked subtrees (or those matching a `--expect-prefix`/`--expect-list`) with no file on disk, and exit 1 on any MISSING.
round1_area_findings.vreason: The behaviour is real, but it is the documented contract, and the failure scenario is caught elsewhere. (1) The module docstring (lines 6-7) and CHANGELOG.md:74-76 say --check verifies 'every data file under DATA_ROOT' and exits 1 on 'any mismatch or unlisted file'. The docs never claim that missing rows are detected. (2) experiments/datasets.tsv is a global manifest: 80 rows covering pbmc3k, 66 cellxgene files, cistarget and references across several experiments. Experiment data roots hold subsets (LM-1's root holds 50 files), so flagging every absent row as MISSING would fail on every root. Missing-row detection is impossible without an expected list, which is the extension the finding itself proposes. (3) The only registered gate that uses it, EXP-20260926-LM-1 line 69, reads 'must exit 0: 50 files': it carries the expected count explicitly. The launch and the reproduction both recorded ok=30 ok-eol=20 (=50). (4) A failed download is not silent: fetch_cellxgene._write_and_fetch does not catch urlopen errors, so the fetch aborts with a traceback and a non-zero exit. An interrupted write leaves a partial data.h5ad, which --check reports as MISMATCH. (5) A missing dataset would also show up as n below 20 in REPORT_REAL.md.

round1_area_findings.title: Slurm work directory is not job-unique for non-array jobs (gb_engine_0_0), so jobs on the same node share and delete each other's folder
round1_area_findings.evidence: `WORK="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gb_engine_${SLURM_ARRAY_JOB_ID:-0}_${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID:-0}"` becomes `/tmp/gb_engine_0_0` for every non-array submission, and registered experiments are submitted that way (EXP-20260926-LM-1, CHUNK=100000). Line 64 runs `rm -rf "$WORK"`, and run_real_task runs `shutil.rmtree(work / task_id)` before and after each task.
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: Two team members' non-array jobs land on the same compute node with the default TMPDIR (/tmp, the default that filled up in LM-1 deviation 1). The second user cannot create subfolders in the first user's /tmp/gb_engine_0_0, so every task becomes a PermissionError row. Resume then treats those rows as final (see the resume finding). One user's cleanup can also remove folders another job still uses.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: Use `${SLURM_JOB_ID}` (and the user) in the path, e.g. `WORK="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gb_engine_${USER}_${SLURM_JOB_ID:-$$}_${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID:-0}"`.
round1_area_findings.vreason: hpc/engine_bench.sbatch:41 builds WORK from SLURM_ARRAY_JOB_ID and SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID only. Every non-array submission therefore gets ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gb_engine_0_0, and non-array is how the registered experiments are submitted (EXP-20260926-LM-1: single job, CHUNK=100000). No doc tells users to set a per-user TMPDIR: docs/HPC.md, hpc/README.md and the grnbench-hpc skill have no TMPDIR guidance, and the sbatch header examples omit it. Only the LM-1 deviation note used TMPDIR=$HOME/gb_tmp. When two team members' non-array jobs overlap on one node with the default /tmp, the second user's run_real_task cannot create <workroot>/<task_id> inside the first user's 755 directory. Each task then gets a PermissionError, caught into the row's 'error' field, and _run_and_save writes the row, so a resubmission skips it. Two parts of the title are overstated. Cross-user deletion cannot happen: /tmp is sticky and the directory is 755, so user B's rm -rf fails. Same-user concurrent jobs are blocked by QOS stud (1 running per user). The realistic effect is an all-error run for the second user. That is loud, not silent: it looks like LM-1 deviation 1 and costs a resubmission. It also assumes the cluster does not set a per-job TMPDIR, which I cannot verify offline. Low severity is right.

round1_area_findings.title: Explicitly stored zeros in sparse input silently break every detection-based QC metric, gate and filter
round1_area_findings.evidence:
qc.py:100-101 and :116 count detection with X.getnnz(); pipeline.py:46 (_nnz_per_gene) and hygiene.py:328 do the same. Nothing in the engine calls eliminate_zeros(); `grep -rn eliminate_zeros src/grnbench` returns nothing. scanpy's own QC does call it. Reproduction (scratchpad/engine/zeros_repro.py): the same 300x2000 Poisson(0.08) counts (about 150 detected genes per cell) were written twice, once as a plain CSR matrix and once with every entry stored (explicit zeros, `(X != full).nnz == 0`), then run through run_prep(force=True). Output:
  stored entries: plain 46345 | with explicit zeros 600000 | same values: True
  plain -> PrepError ... produced an empty matrix (1 cells x 0 genes)   [299/300 cells correctly removed as < 200 genes]
  explicit zeros: median_genes_per_cell=2000.0 sparsity=0.000 cells kept=300/300
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: Some h5ad files store zeros explicitly: Seurat/R converters, code that sets sparse entries to 0, or rounded ambient-corrected matrices. For such a file, identical counts give a different cleaning. Every cell appears to detect every stored gene, so min_genes_per_cell removes nothing. The cells_below_min_genes and sparsity gates pass instead of failing (a D-004 bypass), undetected genes survive min_cells_per_gene, and the doublet heuristic and the MAD thresholds in autoprep are computed on inflated gene counts. The manifest looks normal.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: In ingest.load_any, after the counts check, call X.eliminate_zeros() on sparse X and on every sparse layer (or use (X > 0).sum(axis=...) in qc/pipeline/hygiene). Add a regression test that loads the same matrix with and without explicit zeros and asserts identical QC metrics.
round1_area_findings.vreason: I checked this at HEAD 13106b1. The engine counts detection by stored entries, not by nonzero values. It does this in qc.py:100-101 (n_genes_cell, n_cells_gene via X.getnnz), in qc.py:116 (sparsity via X.getnnz()), in pipeline.py:46 (_nnz_per_gene, which drives filter_genes at :319 and the per-context filter at :381), and in hygiene.py:328 (doublet_heuristic_fraction). profile._nonzero_values (profile.py:70) also takes X.data as 'non-zero values', so technology_from_counts sees stored zeros as well. Nothing on the path removes stored zeros. load_any (ingest.py:53-94) reads the h5ad as it is written, copies X into layers['counts'] and returns it. eliminate_zeros appears nowhere in src/. The one incidental exception is the duplicate-gene aggregation in _clean_gene_names: its sparse matmul drops zeros, but only when duplicate names exist. No DECISIONS, ATTEMPTS or AGENTS.md entry documents this behaviour, so it is not intentional-and-documented. The trigger is reachable in real use: run_prep, autoprep.diagnose/execute_plan (the real_bench and GUI path) and the h5ad ingest (user uploads, CELLxGENE, .raw.X fallback) all go through load_any. I ran two reproductions of my own, each on the same values with and without stored zeros. The values were identical, yet the QC metrics differed. The cells_below_min_genes gate went from FAIL to PASS, which bypasses the D-004 fail-loudly gate. The sparsity warning disappeared. The recommended strategy changed from pseudobulk to pearson_residuals. On severity: the committed results cannot be shown to be affected. The real datasets are not available locally, and the usual sources (10x h5/MTX, CellRanger, loom, dense tables, which pass through sparsify_if_dense on a fresh CSR) normally store no zeros. So this is not a blocker or high. Medium fits: wrong behaviour in the main ingest/QC path, triggered by a specific but realistic kind of input, e.g. a file where values were zeroed in place or written by a converter that keeps zeros. The suggested fix is correct: call eliminate_zeros() on sparse X and on every sparse layer in load_any before _ensure_counts_backed, or count detection with (X > 0). Add a regression test that compares QC with and without stored zeros.

round1_area_findings.title: High-mito tissue relaxation uses substring matching, so brain, adrenal and 'pediatric' datasets silently get the 60% mito gate
round1_area_findings.evidence:
autoprep.py:47-48: HIGH_MITO_TISSUES = ("liver","hepat","heart","cardi","myocard","atri","ventric","septum","kidney","renal","nephr","muscle","brown adipose"); line 349: `if any(k in tissue for k in HIGH_MITO_TISSUES)`. Substring hits: 'adrenal gland'->renal, 'subventricular zone'/'lateral ventricle'/'cerebral ventricle choroid plexus'->ventric, 'lateral septum'->septum, 'pediatric bone marrow'/'psychiatric cohort ...'->atri. End-to-end reproduction (scratchpad/engine/mito_repro.py): identical synthetic counts with median mito 55.1%, only obs['tissue'] changed. diagnose -> plan_preprocessing -> execute_plan gives:
  'lung': mito_fail=None force=False error=PrepError: QC gate failure(s) - mito_fraction ...
  'adrenal gland': mito_fail=60.0 force=False error=None
  'subventricular zone': mito_fail=60.0 force=False error=None
  'lateral septum': mito_fail=60.0 force=False error=None
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: A damaged brain-region dataset (SVZ, lateral ventricle, septum) or an adrenal-gland dataset with median mito above 25% passes the dataset-level gate without --force, and the plan gives no mito warning. D-004 (fail loudly) and A-020 ('fail-loudly stays the default elsewhere') require a refusal here. No LM-2 dataset hits a false positive today, so this is a latent product bug.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: Match whole words or ontology terms, e.g. re.search(r'\b(liver|hepat\w*|heart|cardiac|myocardi\w*|atri(al|um|oventricular)|kidney|renal|nephr\w*|skeletal muscle|muscle|brown adipose)\b', tissue). Accept 'ventricle'/'septum' only together with a cardiac term, or use UBERON IDs from obs['tissue_ontology_term_id']. Add negative tests for 'adrenal gland', 'subventricular zone' and 'lateral septum'.
round1_area_findings.vreason:
At HEAD 13106b1, src/grnbench/autoprep.py:47-48 defines HIGH_MITO_TISSUES as bare fragments ("atri", "ventric", "septum", "renal", ...). Line 349 applies them with a plain substring test, `any(k in tissue for k in HIGH_MITO_TISSUES)`. The tissue string comes straight from the lower-cased majority value of obs['tissue'] (context.py:232-234, weight 3) or from free text matching 'tissue: ...' (context.py:177). CELLxGENE UBERON labels such as 'adrenal gland', 'lateral ventricle', 'subventricular zone' and 'choroid plexus of fourth ventricle' therefore reach the matcher unchanged. When it matches, the planner sets mito_fail=60. Lines 359-362 then drop the failing mito_fraction gate from `failing`, so force stays False and execute_plan runs without a PrepError.

No document makes this intentional. A-020 lists liver/heart/kidney/muscle and says "fail-loudly stays the default elsewhere", and D-004 is ACTIVE. The 'atri'/'ventric'/'septum' fragments are clearly meant for cardiac labels (atrium, ventricle, interventricular septum), but they also hit brain regions, 'adrenal' (via 'renal'), 'pediatric', 'psychiatric' and 'matrix'. The plan then writes a false justification into plan.json and the manifest, e.g. "tissue 'pediatric bone marrow' is naturally rich in mitochondrial RNA (Osorio & Cai 2021)". No mito warning is added to plan.warnings.

Severity stays medium, not higher. I checked experiments/datasets.tsv: the only registered tissues that hit the list are true positives (liver, kidney, atrioventricular node). So no committed or confirmatory result is affected. The trigger is still concrete and reachable through the GUI and CLI with real CELLxGENE brain and adrenal datasets. It bypasses a documented fail-loudly gate and records a wrong provenance reason.

The suggested fix (whole-word or ontology-ID matching, plus negative tests for 'adrenal gland', 'subventricular zone' and 'lateral septum') is appropriate. One caveat: 'ventricle'/'septum' should only count next to a cardiac term (e.g. 'heart left ventricle', 'interventricular septum'), or the heart datasets would lose the relaxation.

round1_area_findings.title: Missing/'unknown' cell-type labels become per-cell-type contexts and can push real cell types out
round1_area_findings.evidence:
autoprep.py:450-451 builds contexts from obs[cell_type_key].astype(str).value_counts(), so NaN becomes the string 'nan' and 'unknown' is kept. profile.py:186-189 counts types the same way, which feeds the selector's per_cell_type rule. hygiene.missing_label_mask, the engine's own shared definition, treats both as missing. Reproduction (scratchpad/engine/ctx_repro.py): make_demo 1500 cells with 250 labels set to NaN and 250 to 'unknown'. Output:
  contexts: ['cell_type=alpha', 'cell_type=beta', 'cell_type=nan', 'cell_type=unknown']
  profile n_cell_types: 5 with_enough: 5
  {'alpha': 449, 'beta': 348, 'nan': 250, 'unknown': 250, 'gamma': 203}
  engine's own missing-label rule flags: 500 cells
  cell_type=nan None kept 221 cells with cell_type == 'nan'
  cell_type=unknown None kept 215 cells with cell_type == 'unknown'
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: CELLxGENE and author annotations often contain 'unknown' or unannotated cells. The engine then infers a 'network per cell type' from a mixture of unlabelled cells, which is exactly the composition confound per-cell-type inference is meant to avoid. The unlabelled groups count toward MAX_CONTEXTS=4 and displace real types (here 'gamma', 203 cells >= 200, is dropped). They also inflate n_cell_types_with_enough_cells, which drives the selector toward per_cell_type.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: In plan_preprocessing and build_profile, drop levels flagged by hygiene.missing_label_mask before value_counts(). Add a test with NaN/'unknown' labels asserting that they are not contexts and not counted.
round1_area_findings.vreason:
I checked the code at HEAD (13106b1) and reproduced the finding with my own script. autoprep.py:450-451 builds contexts from obs[cell_type_key].astype(str).value_counts() and never filters missing labels. profile.py:186-189 counts types the same way, and its n_cell_types_with_enough_cells feeds selector._context (selector.py:192-196), which scores per_cell_type +3 when there are >=2 such types. The engine already has one shared definition of a missing label, hygiene.missing_label_mask, whose docstring says it is shared "so a cell counted as unlabelled in the report is the same cell that is excluded from a stratum". qc._imbalance_gate and hygiene.audit_obs apply it, and pipeline.py:393-394 says "Missing labels are not a stratum". Context planning does not apply it, so this is an inconsistency, not a design choice. Nothing in DECISIONS.md, ATTEMPTS.md or AGENTS.md documents it as intended.

The path is live. real_bench.run_real_task calls plan_preprocessing, and execute_plan runs through screen_candidates (screen.py:257-261). The GUI (ui/app.py:202, 310) uses the same functions. In the committed EXP-20260926-LM-1 rows, rules_choices.context_scope is per_cell_type for 18 of 20 datasets. CELLxGENE, the source of every real dataset, allows 'unknown' as a cell_type value.

Severity stays medium, not higher. I cannot check whether any of the 20 benchmarked datasets actually has >=200 'unknown' or NaN cells, because the data is on the cluster and the committed results do not list context names. So I cannot show that a headline or confirmatory number changed. What is shown: in a main path, a pooled mixture of unlabelled cells is inferred and reported as a 'cell type' network, and a real cell type loses its slot under MAX_CONTEXTS=4.

The suggested fix is right: drop hygiene.missing_label_mask levels before value_counts() in both plan_preprocessing and build_profile, and add a test.

round1_area_findings.title: Selector picks 'external' options that grnbench cannot run, and the plan silently drops them (for example, no doublet removal at all)
round1_area_findings.evidence:
kb.Option.availability() marks implementation='external' options as available when their R/py dependency is installed (scDblFinder, DoubletFinder, DropletUtils/emptydrops, celda/decontx, SoupX, slingshot). The planner only executes scrublet (line 396: drop_doublets = chosen['doublets'] == 'scrublet') and knee (line 340); ambient and pseudotime choices are never executed. Reproduction (scratchpad/engine/r_env_repro.py, kb._have patched to report R packages as installed):
  reference env: selector doublets = scrublet | drop_doublets = True
  R env: selector doublets = scdblfinder | ambient = decontx | executed: drop_doublets = False | warnings mentioning doublets: []
On the raw_droplets scenario (scratchpad/engine/r_droplets.py): no R -> cell_calling knee, 1190 cells kept; R env -> cell_calling choice emptydrops, plan runs no cell calling -> PrepError: QC gate failure(s) - cells_below_min_genes ... 94.9%
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: On a machine with rpy2 and scDblFinder, which the KB is written to detect, droplet datasets are processed with no doublet removal at all. plan.choices and the manifest still say doublets=scdblfinder, and there is no warning. With DropletUtils installed, unfiltered matrices get no cell calling and every context fails. DecontX, SoupX and slingshot choices are recorded but never applied.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: Until an executor exists, treat implementation='external' as unavailable for plan execution (availability() -> False, 'no grnbench executor'). Alternatively, fall back explicitly: map an unrunnable winner to the best runnable option and add a warning. Add a test that patches kb._have to True and asserts drop_doublets stays True or a warning is emitted.
round1_area_findings.vreason:
I checked the code at HEAD 13106b1 and reproduced the bug myself. kb.Option.availability() (src/grnbench/kb.py:116-125) returns True for implementation='external' as soon as every `requires` entry is present. It never checks whether grnbench can execute the option. The selector (selector.py _Scores.result) picks the best available option. For droplet data with at least 1000 cells, _doublets scores scdblfinder at 2.5 and scrublet at 2. For raw droplet matrices, _cell_calling scores emptydrops at 3 and knee at 2. For ambient RNA, _ambient scores decontx at 2 and none at 1.5.

autoprep.plan_preprocessing only executes the choices it knows. Line 396 sets drop_doublets = (chosen['doublets'] == 'scrublet'). Line 340 adds cell_calling only for 'knee'. ambient_rna and pseudotime never become plan decisions. run_prep (pipeline.py:162-164) only accepts cell_calling='knee'.

Without R, the selector's blocked_by_dependency warning ('best option scDblFinder is unavailable ... using scrublet') tells the user. With R installed, the unrunnable option wins, so that warning never fires. The plan then runs no doublet removal and no cell calling, and says nothing.

Nothing documents this as intentional. The selector docstring says the choice is 'the best available one'. The KB option says 'use_when: droplet data; R available'. Nothing in DECISIONS.md, ATTEMPTS.md or the docs says external options are recorded but not run.

On severity, the project's own paths are not affected. rpy2 is not in requirements/lock-py311.txt or pyproject, the HPC scripts do not install R, and the verification venv has no rpy2, scvi or magic. No committed file under benchmarks/results contains scdblfinder, emptydrops or decontx; rules_doublets only shows scrublet, heuristic and 'not run'. So no headline or confirmatory result is invalidated, and this is not a blocker or high. It is a real risk with a clear trigger in the published product (GUI, real_bench, screen): a user who installs rpy2 plus scDblFinder or DropletUtils. That is medium.

One detail in the finding is slightly off. The run manifest does not name scdblfinder: its steps just lack drop_doublets. The unrun choice is recorded in plan.json and in real_bench's rules_choices, and the GUI decision reads 'Remove doublets (scrublet) = False' with the reason '[doublets = scdblfinder] fewest false positives...'. This does not change the verdict.

Python-only environments are not affected. With scvi installed, solo scores 1 and still loses to scrublet at 2, and scvi_denoised never wins. With the cellbender CLI on raw data, cellbender ties with none at 1.5 and none comes first in the stable sort.

Suggested fix, as the finding says: in the selector, treat implementation='external' as unavailable for execution (reason: 'no grnbench executor'). Otherwise, map an unrunnable winner to the best runnable option and add a warning. Add a test that patches kb._have to return True for 'r:' requirements and asserts that drop_doublets stays True and cell_calling stays 'knee'.

round1_area_findings.title: The 'always varied' context candidate is selected_type (a copy of per_cell_type's first context), never pooled with the recommended cleaning
round1_area_findings.evidence: selector._context (189-200) scores per_cell_type 3.0, selected_type 0.0 and pooled -0.5 (-1 plus the 0.5 default bonus), so the runner-up is selected_type. Selection.candidates(always=('context_scope',)) (selector.py:67-85, used by screen.py:223/252) therefore forces 'context_scope=selected_type'. In autoprep:452-453, selected_type is big[:1], the same first context, with identical run_prep arguments, that per_cell_type already runs. Check: select(profile with 3 large types) -> chosen per_cell_type, runner_up selected_type [('per_cell_type', 3.0), ('selected_type', 0.0), ('pooled', -0.5)]; candidates -> ['recommended', 'context_scope=selected_type', 'gene_filter=min_cells_drop_qc_genes']. Committed results, benchmarks/results/engine-2026-09-24-v2-partial/synthetic/rows: 63/63 datasets where the rules chose per_cell_type screened only 'context_scope=selected_type'. Across benchmarks/results, 'context_scope=selected_type' appears 962 times and 'context_scope=pooled' 12 times. In LM-2, 12/20 auto arms fell back to 'baseline', which is the only pooled pipeline.
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: The docstrings (selector.candidates, screen) and the A-016 lesson say the context is always varied to test per-cell-type against pooled per model, because per-type helps correlation methods and starves MI methods. In practice, 'recommended cleaning + pooled' is never screened when per_cell_type is recommended. The only pooled option is the baseline, which also turns off MAD QC and doublets. Per-model auto-vs-baseline results (for example CLR ties, 12% wins; draft claim C3) therefore mix up 'pooled' with 'no cleaning', and one candidate slot is spent on a near-duplicate.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: For decisions in `always`, choose the alternative among options whose executed plan differs materially: exclude selected_type when per_cell_type is chosen, or always add the pooled variant. Alternatively score selected_type below pooled. Record in the bench which context alternatives were screened, and re-state A-016/C3 once pooled+cleaning is screened.
round1_area_findings.vreason: I could not refute it; I reproduced it both through the selector alone and end to end. In selector._context (selector.py:189-201) a dataset with 2 or more large cell types and no time course scores per_cell_type 3.0, selected_type 0.0 (KB default is 'pooled', so selected_type gets no bonus) and pooled 0.5-1 = -0.5. So the runner-up is selected_type. Selection.candidates(always=('context_scope',)) (selector.py:67-85) forces that runner-up, and screen_candidates uses always_vary=('context_scope',) by default (screen.py:223/252). real_bench.py:267, engine_bench.py:173 and ui/app.py:270 all call it with that default. In autoprep.py:449-461, selected_type is big[:1], the largest type, which is also per_cell_type's first context. context_scope is not in RUN_PREP_KEYS (autoprep.py:49), so run_prep receives identical arguments. My end-to-end run on a simulated 3-type dataset gave a processed.h5ad for 'context_scope=selected_type' that is identical to the recommended plan's first context (same obs, same var, np.array_equal True). The only difference in screening is that rank_candidates averages over 1 context instead of 3. As a result, recommended cleaning combined with pooled cells is never screened in the common case. The only pooled pipeline is the 'baseline' extra (engine_bench.BASELINE: fixed QC, no doublets, pooled, no batch). The committed evidence matches the report. In v2-partial/synthetic, 63 of 63 per_cell_type datasets screened only 'context_scope=selected_type'; across benchmarks/results that string appears 962 times against 12 for 'context_scope=pooled'. In EXP-20260925-LM-2, rules chose per_cell_type for 18 of 20 datasets, and the auto arm fell back to 'baseline' in 12 of 20. The behaviour is not documented as intended. The candidates() docstring and rank_candidates() docstring (screen.py:193-195) justify the forced context alternative as per-cell-type versus pooled ('per-cell-type networks help correlation methods and starve mutual-information ones'), and so does the A-016 lesson. The docstring's literal wording, 'runner-up is always tried', is satisfied, but its stated purpose is not. No test covers this. There is one small overstatement: 'never' has an exception. When the profile detects a time course, pooled gets +2 and becomes the runner-up (reproduced; this probably explains the 2 LM-2 lung rows that screened pooled). A second small inaccuracy: selected_type is a strict subset of per_cell_type, not an exact duplicate, because its screening score comes from one context only. Neither changes the defect. On severity, medium is right and not higher. C4 and C5 (confirmatory, reproduced-computational) compare models paired within the same auto arm, so the candidate set changes which pipeline both models see but does not bias the motif-vs-no-motif contrast. The affected claim is C3 (auto ties baseline per model; status draft), whose reading of auto-vs-baseline mixes up 'pooled' with 'no cleaning'. It also affects the product's model-dependent context screening. A minimal fix: in candidates(), for decisions listed in `always`, add the alternative whose plan differs materially. When per_cell_type is chosen, add pooled (or add pooled and keep selected_type as an uncertain alternative), or score selected_type below pooled. Add a test that select() on a profile with 3 large types yields a 'context_scope=pooled' candidate.
