round1_area_findings.title: Holm family of confirmatory tests is set at report time by a mutable code constant and by data availability, not by the registered family
round1_area_findings.evidence:
Both models_section (real_bench.py:375-386) and texreport.comparisons (texreport.py:151-172) loop over the *current* `real_bench.DECLARED_PAIRS`. They skip a pair when a model is absent or has fewer than 3 units, then Holm-correct only what remains. Scratch script family.py adds one pair among the models already run in LM-2:
  current family 4 pearson_motif pearson_signed pHolm 1.36e-07
  after adding ('motif_prior','pearson_signed'): family 6 pearson_motif pearson_signed pHolm 2.04e-07
Scratch script family2.py (RegDiffusion NaN on 18/20 datasets of LM-1):
  family 2 grnboost2_motif grnboost2 n 20 pHolm 1.82e-10 (registered family = 4 directed hypotheses)
No test pins DECLARED_PAIRS (test_real_bench_combined_names_resolve_to_registered_bases only checks the names are registered).
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: AGENTS section 7 requires regenerating reports from unchanged rows after any analysis fix. If anyone edits DECLARED_PAIRS for a new experiment, a later regeneration silently changes p_Holm in the committed REPORT_REAL.md and latex of EXP-20260925-LM-2, EXP-20260926-LM-1 and the exploratory LM-1 table. Separately, when a model fails on most datasets, the family shrinks below what was registered and the surviving hypotheses are under-corrected.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: Make the family an input read from the record (the 'comparison family' / 'primary comparison' lines), or freeze it per experiment (e.g. `family.json` written at registration next to the record). Always Holm over the registered size and count dropped pairs as p = 1. Add a test that pins the per-experiment family.
round1_area_findings.vreason:
The code clearly shows the mechanism. Both statistics paths, `real_bench.models_section` (benchmarks/real_bench.py:375-386) and `texreport.comparisons` (src/grnbench/texreport.py:145-172), read the current module constant `real_bench.DECLARED_PAIRS`. They keep only pairs whose models are present with n>=3, then run Holm over what is left. Nothing reads the record's 'comparison family' field. `_methods` only prints that field as text, and no test pins the family size: test_real_bench_combined_names_resolve_to_registered_bases checks names only, and test_report_matches_the_committed_real_bench_report checks the mean difference, which does not depend on the family.

Several things make this a realistic risk rather than speculation:
(1) Code offers no way to declare a new experiment's comparisons except editing this shared constant. The next model-comparison experiment (the product is side-by-side model comparison) will naturally edit it.
(2) Both confirmatory records define their family by reference to the constant ('`real_bench.DECLARED_PAIRS` restricted to the models run = {...} = 4 directed hypotheses'). experiments/README.md says the family is 'fixed before the run', but the code does not enforce this.
(3) Three documented paths recompute from HEAD: `paper/make_figures.py`, which rewrites paper/tables/T_models_real_EXP-20260925-LM-1.md on every run; `grnbench report --paper`, which rebuilds C4/C5 sections through build_report -> comparisons; and the AGENTS section 7 regeneration.
(4) Git history shows DECLARED_PAIRS has not been edited since the 2026-09-25 snapshot. At HEAD every committed report and the paper table regenerate byte-identically (family 4, 4, 14), so no committed number is wrong today.

I reproduced the drift. Adding ('motif_prior','pearson_signed') and ('regdiffusion','grnboost2') moves LM-2 to family 6 with pHolm 2.04e-07 and LM-1 to family 6 with pHolm 5.45e-10 and 1.57e-06. The Methods text of the paper draft would still say 4, so the draft would contradict itself.

They get either a different p_Holm (all-pairs family) than the declared family or a hard failure when one model loses a dataset. The confirmatory analysis then deviates from its own registration, or cannot be run as registered.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: Change TEMPLATE, experiments/README rule 2, AGENTS section 7 and START_HERE to name the actual path: `real_bench.py report` / `texreport.comparisons` (compare_units per declared pair, Holm over the declared directed family). Or give `grnbench compare` a `--pairs` option and use it in both places.
round1_area_findings.vreason:
Reproduced on the committed rows. `grnbench compare` (src/grnbench/cli_compare.py) passes the whole unit x method table to `compare_units`, which tests every pair of every method in the input. `n_pairs = n_methods*(n_methods-1)//2`, and Holm runs over `2*n_pairs` directed hypotheses. `scores_from_long` (comparison.py:39-40) refuses any missing cell. There is no option to restrict the test to declared pairs. So the CLI cannot run 'Holm over the family above' unless that family is every pair of a set of methods with complete data.

The path the project actually uses for its confirmatory results is `real_bench.models_section` / `texreport.comparisons`. It runs `compare_units` once per pair in `DECLARED_PAIRS`, drops missing data per pair, and applies `holm_adjust` over the declared directed family. None of these four docs name that path: experiments/TEMPLATE.md:16-17, experiments/README.md:13, AGENTS.md:138 and docs/START_HERE_AGENT_PROMPT.md:162. DECISIONS.md:95 names only `compare_units`. DECISIONS.md:49 describes `grnbench compare` as correcting all pairs, which agrees with the code and so contradicts the TEMPLATE's claim that it tests 'the family above'.

This is not documented as intentional anywhere. The two confirmatory records (LM-2 lines 29-35, LM-1 lines 36-43) avoided the problem by writing 'via `compare_units` for each pair ... Holm over the 4 directed hypotheses'. That wording departs from the template, so the current headline numbers are correct and unaffected.

Why medium and not higher. The trigger is clear: any future confirmatory record that follows the template, and any reproducer who follows AGENTS.md or the template. Two things limit the harm:
- Using a larger all-pairs family makes Holm only more conservative, so it cannot create a false positive.
- Missing data makes the CLI fail loudly with rc 2 instead of silently dropping rows.
The real risk is a mismatch between the registration and the analysis, or a failed reproduction. One workaround a user could reach for is also anti-conservative: running the CLI once per pair gives Holm over 2 hypotheses instead of the declared family. That fits the 'real risk with a clear trigger' / secondary-path definition of medium, not blocker or high.

Minimal fix: change the four doc lines to name the declared-family path (`real_bench.py report` / `texreport.comparisons`: `compare_units` per declared pair, then Holm over the declared directed family). Alternatively, add a `--pairs` option to `grnbench compare` that applies the same per-pair missing-data handling.

round1_area_findings.evidence:
In score_models (real_bench.py:203-216), a failing context appends NaN and sets `out[f'm_{m}_{arm}_error']`. The dataset score is then `np.mean([y for y in v[metric] if np.isfinite(y)])`, so the dataset keeps a finite score from the surviving contexts. models_section drops a dataset only when that score is NaN. Stub reproduction (scratch partial_ctx.py: 2 contexts, spearman_signed raises in context 2 only):
  m_pearson_signed_auto_auprc_ratio 0.9806839745707696   (mean of 2 contexts)
  m_spearman_signed_auto_auprc_ratio 0.835438127090301   (context 1 only)
  m_spearman_signed_auto_error ValueError: 1 genes have 0 variance
Both confirmatory records (EXP-20260926-LM-1.md:32, EXP-20260925-LM-2.md:26) register rule (c): 'a dataset where a model errors is dropped from the pairs involving that model only'. No test covers score_models. I checked every committed rows/*.json: the only m_*_error entries are whole-dataset failures (score NaN), so no committed number is affected.
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: A model fails in some but not all contexts of a dataset, as the per-context RegDiffusion zero-variance error of issue #13 could before #16. The pair then compares the model's mean over k contexts with its partner's mean over all contexts. The comparison is no longer paired within the unit, and the dataset is kept although the registered rule says to drop it.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: If any context errors for a model, set that model's dataset score to NaN (or record n_contexts_scored per model and drop unequal ones). Add a unit test with a stubbed partial failure.
round1_area_findings.vreason:
At HEAD 13106b1 the code does what the finding says. In benchmarks/real_bench.py:203-216, a model that raises in one context gets NaN for that context and an m_<model>_<arm>_error field. The dataset score is then the mean of the finite contexts only (`x = [y for y in v[metric] if np.isfinite(y)]`). _model_matrix (342-348) ignores the *_error columns, and models_section (378) drops a dataset from a pair only when the score is NaN (`mat[[a,b]].dropna()`). The error is printed under 'Model errors', but the dataset is not dropped.

Both confirmatory records register rule (c): 'a dataset where a model errors is dropped from the pairs involving that model only' (EXP-20260926-LM-1.md:32-33, EXP-20260925-LM-2.md:26-27). The primary endpoint is registered as the 'mean over contexts within a dataset' (LM-1.md:14-15). So in this case the code contradicts the registration: it keeps the dataset and reports a mean over a subset of contexts. Nothing in DECISIONS.md, ATTEMPTS.md, experiments/README.md or the score_models docstring documents this. No test covers score_models; the only models_section test (tests/test_motif_methods.py:141) uses whole-dataset NaNs.

The path can really occur. In the committed rows of both experiments, the auto arm has several contexts on 3 of the 20 datasets (auto_n_contexts = 3 on primary-motor-cortex 9b686bb6 and cerebral-cortex 774c18c5, 4 on lung 62315937). The failure in LM-1 depended on the context's data (a gene constant after the 3,000-cell subsample, issue #13). Had it hit a multi-context dataset, it would have been a partial failure.

The only committed m_*_error entries (entorhinal-cortex 06b91002, auto_n_contexts = 1) are whole-dataset failures with NaN scores, so no committed number or verdict is affected. That rules out blocker or high.

One correction to the stated failure scenario: in the confirmatory motif-vs-plain pairs (regdiffusion_motif vs regdiffusion, grnboost2_motif vs grnboost2), a failure of the base model hits both members in the same context. The base run is cached per context, a failed run is not cached, and the motif variant re-runs it and raises again. So both members average over the same surviving contexts, and the pair stays paired within the unit. The 'no longer paired' problem appears only for cross-model declared pairs (regdiffusion vs pearson_signed, grnboost2 vs pearson_signed, pearson_motif vs motif_prior) or when only the combiner fails in one context. The rule (c) violation (dataset kept, n too large, endpoint is a partial mean) applies to every pair. Medium is right: the main scoring path deviates from a registered exclusion rule, the trigger is clear, and no current number changes.

The suggested fix is sound: set a model's dataset score to NaN when any of its scored contexts errored (or record the number of contexts scored per model and require it to match), and add a test with a stubbed partial failure.

round1_area_findings.title: data_manifest.py exits 0 on a missing or empty data root, in both generate and --check modes
round1_area_findings.evidence:
$ python benchmarks/data_manifest.py ~/grnbench_dta_typo | wc -l -> 1 (header only), rc=0
$ python benchmarks/data_manifest.py ./no_such_root --check experiments/datasets.tsv -> 'ok=0 ok-eol=0 MISMATCH=0 UNLISTED=0' rc=0
$ (empty partial_root) --check -> same, rc=0
check() iterates only over files present under root. It never reports manifest rows that are absent, and it does not error on a nonexistent root. EXP-20260926-LM-1.md section 2 uses it as the data gate ('must exit 0: 50 files'). experiments/README rule 3 regenerates provenance with `data_manifest.py DATA_ROOT > experiments/datasets.tsv`.
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: A typo in DATA_ROOT passes the pre-run data gate (exit 0, zero files checked), or truncates experiments/datasets.tsv to its header while exiting successfully.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: Exit non-zero when root does not exist or contains no files. In --check, accept an expected file list or count (e.g. the experiment's datasets file) and report MISSING rows.
round1_area_findings.vreason: check() walks only the files that exist under root and returns 1 only on MISMATCH or UNLISTED. A missing or empty root therefore gives all zeros and exit 0, and generate mode gives a header-only TSV with exit 0. The EXP-20260926-LM-1 record's data gate reads '# must exit 0: 50 files'. A careful reader would see ok=0 in the summary line, which lowers the risk, but the exit-code gate alone passes on a typo. experiments/README's `> experiments/datasets.tsv` would truncate the manifest while exiting 0.
round1_area_findings.vrepro: `python benchmarks/data_manifest.py ./no_such_root --check experiments/datasets.tsv` -> 'ok=0 ok-eol=0 MISMATCH=0 UNLISTED=0' rc=0. The same with an empty directory -> the same output, rc=0. `python benchmarks/data_manifest.py ~/grnbench_dta_typo | wc -l` -> 1, rc=0. EXP-20260926-LM-1.md:69 has 'python benchmarks/data_manifest.py $D --check experiments/datasets.tsv   # must exit 0: 50 files'.

round1_area_findings.vreason: real_bench.models_section calls compare_units() on one two-column pair at a time, so n_pairs = 1 and critical = t.ppf(0.975, n-1). That is an ordinary per-pair interval, not a Bonferroni-simultaneous one over the 7 declared pairs. Recomputing from the committed CSV gives exactly the record's [0.160, 0.297] with k=1; k=7 would give [0.126, 0.331]. The generated table labels it correctly as '95% interval'. CLAIMS C1 says '95% CI 0.16-0.30', not 'simultaneous', so the failure scenario that C1 implies family-wise coverage is overstated. Only the record's word is wrong. The experiment is exploratory and superseded by C4, so low.

round1_area_findings.title: Test modules skip entirely when a hard dependency is missing, hiding the failure that caused issue #2
round1_area_findings.evidence: tests/test_doublet_small_batches.py:21 has a module-level `pytest.importorskip("skimage")`, and tests/test_prep_gaps.py:160 does the same. scikit-image is a core dependency in pyproject.toml `dependencies` and pinned in the lock. Its absence is exactly what made scrublet silently fall back in EXP-20260925-LM-1 (issue #2, PR #3). tests/test_motif_methods.py:15 has a module-level `importorskip("pyarrow")`, which also skips tests that need no pyarrow: test_real_bench_models_section_pairs_over_datasets_only, test_real_bench_combined_names_resolve_to_registered_bases and the #13 regression test_regdiffusion_drops_zero_variance_genes. In the lock venv these run: my targeted run of 7 files gave '98 passed, 1 skipped' (only regdiffusion skipped).
round1_area_findings.failure_scenario: In an environment missing scikit-image or pyarrow, the suite stays green with a few extra skips. The scrublet small-batch tests and the real_bench comparison/declared-family tests silently stop running.
round1_area_findings.suggested_fix: For hard dependencies, import directly or fail. Move pyarrow-free tests out of the module-level importorskip, e.g. apply the skip per test only where pyarrow is used.
round1_area_findings.vreason: The central claim is that without scikit-image the suite stays green with a few extra skips, hiding the issue #2 failure. I hid skimage and pyarrow through a sys.meta_path blocker and ran the three test files. test_prep_gaps.py::test_drop_doublets_uses_scrublet_and_logs_what_it_removed has no importorskip and FAILS ('heuristic' == 'scrublet'), so the issue #2 condition is caught loudly. The small-batch tests do need a working scrublet, so skipping them is reasonable. Also, tests/test_prep_gaps.py:160 is a per-test importorskip, not module-level as the finding implies. One part is true: the module-level pyarrow importorskip in test_motif_methods.py also skips three tests that need no pyarrow. round1_critic_findings.title: The '20 fresh' confirmatory datasets are not independent units: 3 pairs come from the same study, and one dataset is a near-duplicate of an exploratory dataset that generated the hypothesis
round1_critic_findings.evidence:
Exclusion works on dataset-id prefixes only (line 118-120: `d["dataset_id"].lower().startswith(i)`). select() does not deduplicate by collection, and _write_and_fetch drops `collection` from the manifest (cols, line 132). This is why the auditors could not see the problem. From experiments/EXP-20260925-LM-2.datasets.tsv titles plus the committed rows:
(1) AD study 'Molecular characterization of selectively vulnerable neurons in Alzheimer's Disease: EC astrocytes' 06b91002 and '...: SFG astrocytes' b94e3bdf (both 31,990 genes).
(2) Patch-seq M1 'All cells with morphological recordings' 341a0702 (636 cells) and 'All cells with electrophysiological recordings' bf6a5c78 (1,320 cells), both 40,650 genes.
(3) Tabula Muris Senis Smart-seq2 'Kidney - A single-cell transcriptomic atlas characterizes ageing tissues in the mouse' 524179b0 and 'Diaphragm - ...same title' cbd62079 (both 21,025 genes).
The exploratory set that produced C1/H1 (engine-2026-09-25-models/test12) holds sister datasets: patch-seq 8f98c236 (628 cells, 40,650 genes, 24,505,344 B vs 341a0702's 24,598,358 B), SFG bdacc907 (31,990 genes) and TMS aorta 0380ddce (21,025 genes). The near-duplicate scores almost identically in both experiments (my script over the committed rows):
- test12 8f98c236: pearson 1.223, pearson_motif 1.365, lift +0.143
- LM-2 341a0702: pearson 1.235, pearson_motif 1.374, lift +0.139
Sensitivity (scratchpad/critic/cluster_collapse.py, scipy ttest_rel + statsmodels Holm): collapsing the 3 same-study pairs to one unit each still supports every conclusion:
- LM-2 H1: +0.184, n=17, p_Holm 1.12e-06 (registered: n=20, 1.36e-07)
- LM-1 GRNBoost2: +0.129, n=17, 1.01e-08
- LM-1 RegDiffusion: +0.192, n=17, 2.42e-06
Collapsing 4 pairs (adding the two 10x-5-v1 lung subsets) gives n=16, and all AUPRC conclusions still hold.
round1_critic_findings.failure_scenario: CLAIMS C4 says 'On 20 fresh real datasets ... n = 20 datasets', and the paired t assumes 20 independent units. In fact at least 3 units are same-study sister subsets (plausibly sharing donors, and for Patch-seq plausibly sharing cells). One 'fresh' confirmatory dataset re-scores essentially the same data (628 vs 636 cells, same gene space, lift +0.143 vs +0.139) as a dataset in the exploratory set that motivated H1. n and the freshness of the set are overstated, and the planned 'fresh-set rerun' (LM-1 section 5) would repeat the problem because exclusion is by dataset id only. The headline directions survive the collapse, so this is a design/claim-wording defect, not a reversal.
round1_critic_findings.suggested_fix:
1. Keep collection_id and collection_name (and donor ids where available) in manifest.tsv and EXP-*.datasets.tsv.
2. Make --exclude-ids exclude whole collections, and cap selection at one dataset per collection.
3. In the paper, report n as independent studies (or use collection/donor as the unit), and add the cluster-collapsed analysis as a registered sensitivity analysis.
4. Reword C4 from 'fresh' to 'new dataset ids', and disclose the overlap with the exploratory set (8f98c236 / 341a0702, bdacc907 / b94e3bdf, 0380ddce / TMS).

round1_critic_findings.title: Motif prior demotes every target missing from the cisTarget database (e.g. genes kept as Ensembl IDs), and those targets can never be CollecTRI positives: a target-level annotation signal feeds the headline motif lift
round1_critic_findings.evidence:
Mechanism in the code:
- motif_ranks fills every TF x gene with the worst rank (`block = np.full(..., n_total)`, line 283). Only genes matched in the symbol-keyed rankings feather get a real rank, so a gene absent from the DB is tied last for every TF.
- ingest keeps the Ensembl ID for genes without a usable symbol (ingest.py:320).
- real_bench._reference builds the gold by symbol match (real_bench.py:81-84), so such a target can never be a positive.
Committed error-analysis tables (viz/*_false_positives.tsv, top false-positive targets per TF; scratchpad/critic/fp_ensembl_share.py), share of targets that are raw Ensembl IDs:
- LM-2 SFG b94e3bdf: pearson_signed 21.8%, pearson_motif 3.4%, motif_prior 0%
- LM-2 EC 06b91002: pearson_signed 18.4%, pearson_motif 2.3%, motif_prior 0%
- LM-1 b94e3bdf: grnboost2 18.4% vs grnboost2_motif 4.6%; regdiffusion 4.6% vs regdiffusion_motif 0%
- LM-1 06b91002: grnboost2 16.1% vs grnboost2_motif 3.4%
Toy with NO motif information (scratchpad/critic/db_membership.py: random motif ranks, symbol genes in the DB, 'ENSG' genes absent; 10 seeds, weak-signal regime EFF=0.03 matching real AUPRC ratios of about 1.3-1.6). Raising the share of no-symbol targets from 0% to 15% moves:
- motif_prior: 1.065 -> 1.211
- pearson_motif: 1.425 -> 1.555
- pearson_signed: unchanged at 1.576
The prior therefore gains about +0.13-0.15 AUPRC-ratio units from DB membership alone, comparable to H1's +0.18. The existing findings cover only the TF-level part (motif count per TF, motif-less TFs); this target-level channel is not mentioned in any record, claim or doc (grep).
round1_critic_findings.failure_scenario: C4/C5 attribute the AUPRC-ratio gain to motif (sequence) evidence. Part of the gain comes from pushing unlabelable targets to the bottom: genes without a symbol, and more generally genes outside the RefSeq-based ranking DB such as many lncRNAs. Co-expression models rank these targets high, and the reference cannot label them by construction. No arm or universe restriction separates this from target-level motif evidence. The same applies to the 'pearson_motif vs motif_prior' secondary and to the product's advice that the prior 'lifts every model'.
round1_critic_findings.suggested_fix:
Choose one of two controls:
- Evaluate every model on a universe restricted to targets that are labelable and present in the motif DB (symbol in the reference namespace and in the rankings columns), and report the lift there.
- Add a registered control arm that ranks targets only by DB membership (0 = in DB, worst = absent) combined with the base by the same rank product.
In either case, record the share of universe targets missing from the DB per dataset in the rows, and state this channel in C4/C5 alongside the TF-level confound.

round1_critic_findings.title: --from-manifest refetch writes a different README.md than the original fetch; README.md is read as engine evidence, but data_manifest skips it, so the 'bytes are pinned' check does not cover all engine inputs
round1_critic_findings.evidence:
Two README variants reach the engine:
- The original fetch writes README.md = title + 'Collection: <collection_name>' + citation (line 68 keeps them from the listing; lines 153-154 write them).
- --from-manifest sets collection="" and citation="" (line 111), and the manifest cannot carry them (cols, line 132).
The context reader parses README*/*.md next to the data as evidence (context.py:29, 340). data_manifest.py SKIPs README.md in both generate and --check (line 31).
Reproduced in scratch: fetch_cellxgene._write_and_fetch for one row, then main(['--from-manifest', ...]) for the same row. Output: 'README identical: False', 'truth identical: True'.
- original: 'All cells with electrophysiological recordings\n\nCollection: Phenotypic variation ... in mouse motor cortex ...\nPublication: ...'
- from-manifest: 'All cells with electrophysiological recordings\n\nCollection: \n\n'
extract_from_text gives [('organism','mouse',1)] for the original and [] for the refetch. EXP-20260926-LM-1 section 2 fetched its data with exactly this --from-manifest command, and its check 'must exit 0: 50 files' passes regardless of README content.
round1_critic_findings.failure_scenario:
A reproduction from the record (or LM-1 on the cluster) gives the engine different README evidence from the original LM-2 run. If a collection name or citation contains a rule keyword, the plan changes:
- 'differentiation' or 'time course' flips time_course, which gives pooled +2 in selector._context plus pseudotime choices;
- a platform or organism word changes the votes.
The candidate pipelines and the auto arm then change, while the sha256 check reports the data as identical. I could not show that any committed LM-1 row changed this way: the original READMEs are not in the repo.
round1_critic_findings.suggested_fix:
Choose one:
- Keep collection_name and citation in manifest.tsv / EXP-*.datasets.tsv, and have --from-manifest write the byte-identical README.
- Or hash README.md too (remove it from data_manifest.SKIP).
- Or have context.gather ignore the fetch-generated README, since truth.json already carries the curated metadata and is separately a known leak.

units_facts.reasoning:
I checked the facts against the committed files and could not refute any of the central claims.

1) Same-study pairs (experiments/EXP-20260925-LM-2.datasets.tsv)
- AD pair: the titles make this certain. 06b91002 is "Molecular characterization of selectively vulnerable neurons in Alzheimer's Disease: EC astrocytes" and b94e3bdf is the same title with ": SFG astrocytes". Both are 10x 3' v2, human, nucleus, 31990 genes, 27002 reference edges.
- TMS pair: also certain from the titles. 524179b0 is "Kidney - A single-cell transcriptomic atlas characterizes ageing tissues in the mouse - Smart-seq2" and cbd62079 is "Diaphragm — A single-cell transcriptomic atlas characterizes ageing tissues in the mouse". Both have 21025 genes and 27064 reference edges.
- Patch-seq pair: this one is inferred, not confirmed. The titles "All cells with morphological recordings" (341a0702, 636 cells) and "All cells with electrophysiological recordings" (bf6a5c78, 1320 cells) carry no study name. The inference rests on the same assay, organism and tissue, the same 40650 genes and the same 27590 reference edges.
- These three pairs are exactly the three shared gene spaces among the 20 datasets.
- No collection field exists in any committed file, and the CELLxGENE API is blocked from here (403), so no pairing is backed by a collection id.

2) 341a0702 as a near-duplicate of 8f98c236 (exploratory, in test12 of EXP-20260925-LM-1, the run whose +0.229 motivated H1)
- Size: 628 vs 636 cells (+1.3%) and 24,505,344 vs 24,598,358 bytes (+0.38%).
- Pipeline: identical rules_choices, context counts, n_genes and reference_edges.
- Scores: in pearson_motif minus pearson_signed (auto AUPRC ratio), 8f98c236 gives +0.1425 and 341a0702 gives +0.1394, which matches the critic's +0.143 vs +0.139.
- Nearest-neighbour scan (my nearest.py): 341a0702~8f98c236 is by far the closest pair. The largest difference over 10 Pearson-family fields is 0.023, and over the 4 GRNBoost2/RegDiffusion fields 0.024. The next-closest pair across the two sets differs by 0.099, and the closest pair within LM-2 by 0.078. Its same-study sibling bf6a5c78 differs by 0.07-0.2.
- This is circumstantial but strong. It is "plausibly the same or largely overlapping cells", not proven: no titles or cell barcodes for 8f98c236 are in the repo.

3) Code
- fetch_cellxgene.py:118-120 excludes only by dataset-id prefix.
- select() (lines 54-86) has no collection-level deduplication. It sorts by file size and round-robins over (assay, organism). This is why 8f98c236 (smallest Patch-seq file) was excluded and 341a0702 (next smallest by 93 KB) was picked.
- The manifest columns at lines 132-133 omit collection.

4) Claim C4 (paper/CLAIMS.md:16) says "On 20 fresh real datasets ... n = 20". Confirmed.

5) Disclosure
- I searched experiments/*.md, paper/, .projectos/STATE.md, DECISIONS, ATTEMPTS, REPORT_REAL.md and CHANGELOG for patch-seq, alzheimer, tabula, collection, same study, duplicate and independen. None discloses the same-study pairs or the overlap with the exploratory set.
- EXP-20260926-LM-1.md even says the exploratory estimates "come from 12 other datasets", which is true only at the id level.
- tests/test_engine.py:283 pairs 8f98c236 with 341a0702 as test ids, so both ids were in view, but nothing flags them.

6) How "fresh" is defined
- LM-2 section 1 defines it operationally: the 31 dataset ids used by any earlier experiment were excluded before selection (EXP-20260925-LM-2.excluded_ids.txt, which includes 8f98c236).
- EXP-20260926-LM-1.md:190 says "datasets never used by any experiment".
- So by the record's own id-level definition, 341a0702 counts as fresh. The finding's point, that id-level freshness is not cell-level or study-level freshness, stands.

7) Sensitivity
- I reran critic/cluster_collapse.py and got exactly the critic's numbers:
  - LM-2 H1: +0.184, n=17, p_Holm 1.12e-06
  - GRNBoost2: +0.129, n=17, p_Holm 1.01e-08
  - RegDiffusion: +0.192, n=17, p_Holm 2.42e-06
- Dropping 341a0702 alone gives +0.185, n=19, two-sided p 1.7e-07 (unadjusted).
- The conclusions survive. The defect is in the reporting and independence framing, not in the results, so medium stays appropriate for a pre-registered headline claim.

8) Extra evidence, not in the finding (inferred from shared gene counts only)
- The exploratory and earlier sets appear to contain siblings of the confirmatory studies:
  - bdacc907 (SFG, 10x 3' v2 human, 31990 genes, in test12) and 9f1049ac (EC, 31990 genes, engine-2026-09-24) look like the AD study.
  - 0380ddce (Smart-seq2 mouse aorta, 21025 genes, in test12) looks like TMS.
  - 989a76f9 / 8ef59750 share 20208 genes.
  - 182f8181 / 20de8570 share 32381 genes.
- If so, study-level overlap with the exploratory set goes beyond 341a0702.

I could not refute the finding. I measured the effect on the real confirmatory datasets through the real grnbench code path. It is real and nothing in the records controls for it. It is smaller than the finding implies, and it does not reverse C4 or C5.

1. The code does what the finding says (exact lines read):
- cistarget.py:283 is `block = np.full((len(tfs), len(genes)), n_total, ...)`.
- Only genes matched case-insensitively in the feather get a rank (cistarget.py:115).
- ingest.py:320 keeps the Ensembl ID where the symbol is unusable.
- real_bench.py:81-84 builds the gold by upper-case symbol match.
- CollecTRI has 0 Ensembl-ID targets (snapshot check), so ENSG-named targets can never be positives.
- `grep` for shuffle/permut/membership/coverage/absent/ensembl in EXP-20260925-LM-2.md, EXP-20260926-LM-1.md and CLAIMS.md finds nothing, so no control separates the effect.

2. My own toy (not the critic's) uses the real pearson_signed, motif_rank_product, motif_prior and evaluate_ranking on an explicit universe.
- Setup: 2 fake feathers, random ranks, 1-60 motifs per TF, 10% of TFs motif-less, base AUPRC ratio about 1.4. Each seed is scored twice: once as the code runs, once with a control DB that covers every gene using the same rank matrix.
- Membership-only lift at 5 / 10 / 20% absent share: +0.040 / +0.085 / +0.202 (8 seeds, tight ranges).
- The lift is the same whether the absent genes are neutral, weakly expressed, or TF-driven, so the critic's driven design is not needed.
- If the absent genes can be gold at the same rate as present genes, the lift is about 0 (+0.005 to +0.008). The effect comes from absent genes being unlabelable.
- With informative motifs the membership part grows: +0.10 and +0.13 at 10% share.

3. Real data, same paired design, through `real_bench.score_models`. I fetched 12 of the 13 human LM-2 h5ads from the CELLxGENE census S3 (2025-11-10, schema 7.0.0); 805832dc is not in the census. I used a CollecTRI snapshot from decoupler 2.2.0.
- The reconstruction is faithful: reference pair counts equal the committed `reference_edges` on all 12 datasets. Baseline Pearson AUPRC ratio is within 0.001 of the committed value on all 12, and GRNBoost2 matches exactly on the 9 datasets I ran.
- ENSG-named share of the evaluated universe (TFs plus 1000 HVGs): 0 to 11.2%, mean 5.6%.
- **Pearson (C4):** membership-only lift averages +0.042 (range 0 to +0.085). The observed baseline-arm lift on the same 12 datasets is +0.202, so about 21% is membership. A one-motif-per-TF design gives +0.043, so the result does not depend on the motif design. Per dataset the share is up to 60% (eec804b9: 0.085 of 0.140) and 50% (bdc7e498).
- **GRNBoost2 (C5):** +0.0195 of +0.131, about 15%.
- **Adjusted lifts:** after subtracting membership, every dataset stays positive (Pearson mean +0.160, t=6.92, p=2.5e-5; GRNBoost2 mean +0.111). The direction of C4 and C5 survives; the size and the "sequence evidence" reading are inflated.
- **motif_prior:** the sequence-only arm gains +0.057 from membership alone, so the declared pearson_motif vs motif_prior comparison is affected too.
- **Mouse:** in the 4 mouse datasets I could fetch, the universe has 0 ENSMUSG-named genes, so the effect is 0 there.
- **Pooled over C4's 20 datasets:** about +0.025 of +0.182 (14%). 4 datasets are unmeasured because they are not in the census.
- **Upper bound:** if every non-protein-coding symbol gene were also absent from the DB, the Pearson membership lift would be +0.123 (61%). That overstates it: LINC01392 and ZBTB46-AS1 are in the DB, since they appear as motif_prior false positives at rank 0.
- **Pattern in the data:** the observed lift is lower in the 3 datasets with no ENSG genes (0.116) than in the other 9 (0.231). Spearman rho is 0.47, p=0.13, so this is only suggestive.

4. Can a gene with a symbol but missing from the DB be a positive? By the code, yes: the gold matches any symbol and the prior demotes any unmatched gene. In practice it is rare.
- In CollecTRI, 6586 of 6675 targets (99.3% of edges) are protein-coding. The non-coding exceptions are few, for example IGKC, IGHM, IGHG1 and MIR17HG.
- Non-protein-coding symbol genes make up 1.9-22.6% of the universe (lncRNA, plus IG/TR genes in the lung datasets), but only 0-7 of them per universe are CollecTRI targets. Gold pairs with a non-coding target: SFG 2/3324, EC 0/3293, prostate 6/6298.
- So the mechanism is not limited to Ensembl IDs. Any symbol lncRNA missing from the DB behaves like an ENSG gene and adds lift. The rare demoted positives, and protein-coding genes renamed since the DB was built, would push the other way; I could not check either because aertslab returns 403.

3. "motif_prior 0%" is true by construction, so it adds no evidence.

4. "Demotes every target missing from the DB" overstates it. The rank product only partly demotes these targets: Ensembl IDs remain among top false positives for HNF4A and PPARG (SFG) and ESR1 and RELA (EC) under pearson_motif. For TFs without motifs there is no within-TF demotion at all.

5. No committed quantity bounds how many universe targets are Ensembl IDs or missing from the DB. Rows keep only auprc_ratio and epr; there is no n_candidates, prevalence or n_gold.

6. Where real data can speak, it goes against this being the main driver. Prostate keeps 68-74% of the mean C4/C5 lift with at most 2.5% Ensembl false positives. The lift does not track n_genes_in across the 20 datasets.

7. Prevalence is identical for base and motif models within each arm and context, so the lift is not a prevalence artifact. The TF-level confound cannot explain the shift in the FP tables, but committed data cannot separate it from membership effects in the AUPRC lift.

readme.reasoning:
Every factual part of the finding holds up, and I found evidence in the committed rows that the README drift really did change engine behaviour between LM-2 and LM-1. It is not only a theoretical gap.

1) Code paths (exact reads).
- fetch_cellxgene.py:110-111 sets collection="" and citation="" for --from-manifest. Lines 153-154 write README.md as the title, then "Collection: {collection}", then the citation.
- context.py:29 README_PATTERNS matches README.md, and also *.json, so truth.json is read too. context.py:331 discovers the files and :340 runs extract_from_text on them.
- real_bench.py:237 calls diagnose(task["path"]), which calls build_context(path, adata) with discover=True (autoprep.py:199).
- data_manifest.py:31 SKIP contains README.md. It is applied in generate (:52) and in check (:69).
- experiments/datasets.tsv has 33 data.h5ad rows, 33 truth.json rows and 0 README rows.
- LM-1 record line 65 fetches with --from-manifest. The cluster check reported ok-eol=20, which fits truth.json being freshly written on Linux. LM-2 ran at 67ca880, which fetched through the listing path and so wrote the collection name and citation. fetch_cellxgene.py at 84f28e1 is identical to HEAD.

2) Offline reproduction.
- I monkeypatched urlopen and built a fake listing from the committed LM-2 manifest.
- Both the listing path and --from-manifest write a manifest.tsv byte-identical to EXP-20260925-LM-2.datasets.tsv. data.h5ad and truth.json are identical in 20/20 folders.
- README.md differs in 20/20 folders. The --from-manifest version is 'title\n\nCollection: \n\n'.
- I pinned the listing-path copy with data_manifest.py, then ran --check on the --from-manifest copy: ok=40 MISMATCH=0, exit 0.

3) Plan impact on the committed data.
- selector.py, profile.py, context.py, autoprep.py, screen.py and ingest.py are the same git blobs at 67ca880 (LM-2) and 84f28e1 (LM-1). kb.py only changed scrublet text. data.h5ad and truth.json are pinned. That leaves README.md as the only differing input to planning.
- Across all 20 datasets these fields are identical between the runs: rules_choices, got_organism, got_technology, reference_edges, n_cells_in.
- Warnings: n_warnings is computed at plan time, before any doublet call, so PR #11 cannot affect it. It dropped by exactly 1 in 5 datasets:
  - 9b686bb6: 3 to 2
  - e2529f66: 4 to 3
  - 62315937: 5 to 4
  - 7b3368a5: 5 to 4
  - 805832dc: 3 to 2
  - 9b686bb6 and e2529f66 are not PR #11 datasets.
- Stand-in test for the organism warning: I placed identical synthetic CELLxGENE-like data next to each README variant and ran the real diagnose and plan_preprocessing. With the collection names I infer for 9b686bb6 and e2529f66 (Bakken 2021, Emont 2022, both naming the other species), the listing-path README adds exactly one warning, "Sources disagree on organism", and choices stay identical.
- Screening candidates: a 'context_scope=pooled' candidate appears only in LM-2 rows, and only for the two lung datasets. With per_cell_type recommended, the _context scores (pooled = 0.5-1+2*time_course vs selected_type = 0) make pooled the runner-up only if time_course=yes.
  - In LM-1, 62315937 has 'context_scope=selected_type' instead, meaning time_course=no.
  - 7b3368a5's auto arm went from context_scope=pooled (LM-2) to baseline (LM-1).
- Stand-in test for time_course: adding 'differentiation' to the collection line flips time_course. It adds one warning ("pseudotime: best option 'Diffusion pseudotime' is unavailable") and changes the candidates from selected_type to pooled plus pseudotime=provided, with rules_choices unchanged.
- Conclusion on the lung datasets: LM-2's README text set time_course=yes there, and LM-1's blank README did not. The LM-1 record puts all LM-1 vs LM-2 differences down to PR #11, so this cause is unrecorded. Separately, all 20 datasets show cross-machine numeric drift (06b91002 rules_eval_mean 1.1673 vs 1.1567), which explains eec804b9's auto_noref flip.

4) Severity.
- H1/H2 compare pairs within LM-1 on a shared auto arm, so the drift does not bias them. Dropping both lung datasets gives p=2.0e-06 (H1) and 8.1e-10 (H2). Setting both to the worst observed difference gives p=6.3e-06 and 4.3e-09.
- The fetch in LM-1's record is deterministic.
- The real risk is reproducibility: a copy fetched by the listing path (LM-2's data, or a renamed collection) passes --check but screens different candidates.
- Low stays right for the claims, but the effect is real, not hypothetical.

readme.corrections:
No fact in the finding is wrong. Nuances:
(1) The finding understates the impact. The README drift is visible in the committed rows:
- n_warnings fell by 1 in 5 datasets, 2 of which PR #11 does not touch.
- On the two lung datasets (62315937, 7b3368a5) the time_course flag was lost, which removed the 'context_scope=pooled' screening candidate. For 7b3368a5 this changed the auto arm from context_scope=pooled to baseline.
- The LM-1 record puts all LM-1 vs LM-2 differences down to PR #11, which is incomplete.
- H1/H2 still hold (p <= 6.3e-06 under worst-case handling of those datasets).
(2) The LM-1 record's sha256 statement explicitly names only data.h5ad and truth.json (lines 20-21). So the record does not literally claim README is pinned. The gap is that its "(2) their bytes are pinned by sha256, so the cluster copy is checked, not trusted" treats those files as the whole engine input.
(3) The evidence that LM-1 used --from-manifest is the record's own command (line 65) plus the ok-eol=20 line-ending signature. No cluster log was inspected. The row evidence (lost time_course on the lung datasets) is consistent with blank collection names.
(4) The --from-manifest README is not empty: it keeps the title and blanks only the collection line and the citation.
(5) Aside: README_PATTERNS also matches truth.json, which is pinned, so the curated ground truth is itself read as weak context evidence.

experiments.details: Point 4, the ok-eol clause of exclusion rule (a): the clause ('for truth.json a difference in line endings only is accepted, data_manifest.py --check reports it as ok-eol') is already in the registration commit eee1171. The code that implements it arrived in the same commit: the -S'ok-eol' pickaxe gives eee1171 as the first commit, with TEXT_SUFFIXES and _eol_sha, plus a test asserting 'ok=1 ok-eol=1'. It was on GitHub at 2026-09-26T19:32:39Z (server time). The cluster data check that needed it came later. Issue comments say HPC access only started working at 00:27:36Z on 2026-09-27, and sync was still failing with 'Disk quota exceeded' then. The check result (ok=30 ok-eol=20 MISMATCH=0 UNLISTED=0) first appears in the launch comment at 01:38:52Z and in 34c4d21 (pushed 01:43:29Z). So the clause predates the check by more than 5 h, and predates the first job by about 6 h. The need was predictable mechanically, not a data-driven surprise. fetch_cellxgene.py writes truth.json with Path.write_text, which uses platform newlines. I recomputed the entorhinal-cortex truth.json: CRLF gives 106 bytes, sha 3cb864b2..., which equals the value in experiments/datasets.tsv; LF gives 101 bytes, sha a344a843.... So the manifest holds Windows CRLF hashes, and a Linux fetch cannot match any of the 20 truth.json files. Without the clause, rule (a) would have excluded all 20 datasets. Caveats: (a) the code accepts EOL-only differences for every .json/.tsv/.txt/.tbl file, which is broader than the registered text ('truth.json' only). The reported ok-eol=20 equals the number of truth.json files, so it is consistent in practice, but that count is an author claim from the cluster that I cannot rerun (no HPC). (b) I cannot establish from git or GitHub that no cluster data check happened before registration; the only evidence is the author's comments. Other minor issues: (1) Section 2 pre-committed to merging PR #11, but PR #11 received a commit after the registration: daea891, pushed 2026-09-26T19:34:46Z, 2 min after eee1171. It changes hygiene.detect_doublets bookkeeping: info fields, a no-copy path when all cells are scored, cleanup of the temporary obs column, and copying uns. The same seed and data should give the same scores; I checked this by inspection only, not by running it. (2) Rule (d) names 'TIMEOUT or out of memory', but it was applied to ENOSPC (job 670900: all 20 rows were errors, nothing scored). This is recorded as dated deviation 1, and section 1 was not rewritten. (3) Rule (c) was applied to entorhinal-cortex RegDiffusion ('1 genes have 0 variance'), giving n=19 for H1 as the rule allows. The adapter fix (#16) was merged after the results, and the rows were not re-run. (4) The datasets are not blind to the LM-2 Pearson results; section 1 says so itself. No committed earlier results folder mentions any of the 20 dataset ids. Seeds were checked at CODE_COMMIT: screen_candidates seed=0 -> execute_plan -> run_prep -> detect_doublets (scrublet seed 0), regdiffusion_runner n_steps=1000 seed=0, tree_methods seed=42. These match section 1. Clock consistency: author dates run 2-3 s after the server push times for 8e091f6, 67ca880, eee1171 and 84f28e1, so no backdating is visible.
